articles.title: NBA, Nike Reveal New 'Specter' Edition Jerseys in Video, Photos Ahead of 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers and seven other teams are going to have a new alternative look during the 2026-27 campaign.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers and seven other teams are going to have a new alternative look during the 2026-27 campaign.

Nike and the NBA unveiled new "Specter" edition jerseys Wednesday, with the Lakers, Boston Celtics, Philadelphia 76ers, Golden State Warriors, Detroit Pistons, Atlanta Hawks and Sacramento Kings all set to rock the new threads this coming season.

Here's a look at the new jerseys, highlighted by a Luka Doncic Lakers jersey being modeled on the runway:

The NBA announced Wednesday that Nike was issuing new Standard Issue Collection jerseys for all 30 teams and new NBA Specter Edition uniforms "for the teams who trace their roots back to the earliest chapters of the league."

"Bringing forward the same obsession with the game that defines the NBA Standard Issue collection, each uniform features details inspired by the franchises' history, city heritage and fan culture," the NBA said in an announcement.

The 2026-27 NBA season is set to open on October 20 with the Celtics, Pistons, 76ers, Knicks, Thunder and Spurs all in action.

articles.title: LeBron James’ son Bronny James acknowledges new Lakers leader Luka Doncic who sponsored a Slovenia trip for teammates
articles.summary: NBA News: Bronny James has a clearer picture of where he can help the Los Angeles Lakers as he prepares for another season in a changing roster. His summer incl.
articles.body: Bronny James has a clearer picture of where he can help the Los Angeles Lakers as he prepares for another season in a changing roster. His summer included time with Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves, along with a team trip to Slovenia that gave the young guard a chance to build stronger connections with his teammates. For Bronny, the trip was not only about basketball. It also offered a close look at Doncic's home country and showed how the Lakers' new leader helped the group make the most of its time there.Doncic hosted the Lakers during their Slovenia visit, helping the team experience Ljubljana, Lake Bled and other parts of the country. Bronny spoke warmly about the trip while also outlining what he hopes to bring to Los Angeles this season. With several guards competing for minutes, he sees value in becoming a dependable secondary ball handler who can also play without the ball, knock down shots and defend.Bronny James praises new Lakers leader Luka DoncicThe Lakers' Slovenia trip mixed basketball work with time away from the court, giving a reshaped roster an opportunity to develop chemistry. Luka Doncic played host in his native country and helped teammates find some of the best spots during their stay.leBron James' son, Bronny James, recently shared that he appreciated the role Doncic played."We were with [Dončić]. He was hooking us up and getting us in the right places in Slovenia, seeing the most out of the country," James said during an interview on ESPN LA 710.Bronny also highlighted Ljubljana and Lake Bled, along with the scenery surrounding the area."[Slovenia is] great… The city [of Ljubljana] was great, we had the castle that was close to us. And then we went to Lake Bled, which was great. The castle there, and then we played the [golf] course over there near Bled,” he continued, adding, “I wanna go back to go to the Alps and stuff like that. The scenery and everything was great."The experience also helped the Lakers spend meaningful time together before the regular season.Bronny James explains his Lakers role in the coming seasonBronny enters the season facing competition for a place in the Lakers' rotation. Other than Doncic and Reaves, Los Angeles has Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton, Jaden Hardy and Cameron Carr available in the backcourt.Bronny has identified a supporting role beside the team's established creators: "I can be a secondary ball handler to Luka and AR and generate whatever offense, catch-and-shoots, pick-and-roll offense, and stuff like that," James told Mason & Ireland.His defense could also help his case for playing time. The hosts pointed out how much attention his defensive work has received, giving him a potential path to minutes alongside Doncic and Reaves.Bronny still has offensive areas to improve. He needs a tighter handle, quicker decisions and greater consistency as a catch-and-shoot player. Those improvements could allow him to move between roles instead of being tied to one position. Bronny is finally set to prove is worth without the shadow of his father as many critics have shared before.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: $80 million rich 6-foot-10 new Kings star could earn $3.5 million in his big NBA return after a one-year hiatus
articles.summary: NBA News: Ben Simmons hasn't played an NBA game in over a year, and Sacramento just bet $3.5 million that the time off actually worked. The Kings signed the thr.
articles.body: Ben Simmons hasn't played an NBA game in over a year, and Sacramento just bet $3.5 million that the time off actually worked. The Kings signed the three-time All-Star to a one-year, non-guaranteed deal, with real money riding on whether he's still good enough to stick.The number that's getting astonishing hype is $1 million. That's what Simmons pockets simply for making the Kings' roster when they open the season against the Clippers on October 21. Everything else in this contract is built around him earning a spot, not keeping one.How much money will Ben Simmons make in his new Kings tenure?According to NBA reporter Michael Scotto, Simmons' deal tops out at $3.5 million, but it's non-guaranteed, which means Sacramento can move on without much cost if the comeback stalls. Scotto reported Simmons "will earn $1 million" once he survives cuts and reaches opening night.That's the first checkpoint. Everything past it depends on whether a 30-year-old who has battled back and leg problems for years can hold up over an 82-game season. Simmons has a staggering net worth of $80 million, as per Celebrity Net Worth.What role is Sacramento actually giving him?Simmons is set to back up rookie point guard Darius Acuff Jr, the Kings' No. 7 pick, though ESPN and Andscape's Marc J. Spears reported he could end up guarding all five positions depending on matchups. Spears also relayed that people close to Simmons see him as someone who could stay in Sacramento past this season if things click, since he's "a pretty loyal guy" by nature.Simmons spent his year away working on his back and leg injuries and even bought a 50 percent stake in a South Florida fishing club. He told Men's Health he needed distance from the game, saying, "I needed to get away, and have some space, and just find myself again."Does Simmons still have anything left in the tank?Former NBA champion Richard Jefferson isn't ready to write him off. Speaking to ESPN Australia, Jefferson argued "Ben has the talent to be an All-Star this year" if his body cooperates. That's a big if. Simmons hasn't looked like an All-Star since 2020-21, when he averaged 14.3 points, 7.2 rebounds and 6.9 assists a game in Philadelphia.Since then, back surgeries and nerve pain have limited him to just 108 games, and his final stretch with the Nets and Clippers last season produced only 5.0 points and 4.7 rebounds a night. The Kings aren't expecting that version of Simmons back overnight. They're hoping a healthier body and a smaller stage give him room to rebuild.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “I was really stubborn in my earlier..”: How Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry’s motherhood journey became a powerful reminder of just how strong a mother can be
articles.summary: NBA News: Motherhood has given Ayesha Curry some of her happiest moments, but it has also tested her in ways that were difficult to hide. Her third pregnancy in.
articles.body: Motherhood has given Ayesha Curry some of her happiest moments, but it has also tested her in ways that were difficult to hide. Her third pregnancy in 2018 brought repeated hospital stays, severe sickness and exhaustion while she was preparing to welcome another child with Stephen Curry. Years later, those experiences helped her understand motherhood differently.By 2024, Ayesha was expecting her fourth child and looking back at those earlier pregnancies with a different perspective. She had learned that being a strong mother was not about doing everything herself. Sometimes, it meant knowing when to slow down, accept help and give herself some grace. Ayesha Curry pushed through five hospital stays, severe sickness and a difficult road to motherhoodAyesha’s third pregnancy became difficult almost from the start. In February 2018, she explained that she was dealing with hyperemesis gravidarum, a severe pregnancy condition that can cause prolonged nausea, vomiting and exhaustion.The symptoms also took away something that meant a lot to her. Ayesha had built a career around food, yet she could barely eat or cook. In a Feb. 2018 blog post, she wrote, “For the past 4 months, I've barely been able to eat let alone cook. The mere smell of food averts me.” She admitted that the situation had put her “in a funk” and added, “I am truly very, very sad.”The struggle did not disappear quickly. On April 6, 2018, Ayesha revealed that she had already spent five hospital stays since the beginning of the year. Giving an update on Instagram, she wrote, “I've had 5 hospital stays since the New Year and have pretty much been sucking at life.” She then added that she felt she was finally starting “to turn a corner.”That was a brutally honest look at what she was going through. Yet Ayesha kept moving forward and eventually welcomed her son Canon on July 2, 2018. The baby arrived earlier than she and Stephen expected, turning a painful pregnancy chapter into one of the family's biggest moments.But another health challenge followed. On October 5, 2018, Ayesha underwent surgery to remove her thyroid and a cyst. From her hospital bed, she shared an update that simply read, “All went well. God is good. Thank you for your prayers.”Two days later, Stephen Curry also reassured reporters. After the Warriors' open practice at Oracle Arena on October 7, he was asked about Ayesha and said, “We’re good,” before adding, “Thanks for asking.” Ayesha Curry eventually learned that asking for help could make motherhood easierThose experiences clearly stayed with Ayesha. When she became pregnant with her fourth child in 2024, she approached motherhood with a much different mindset.In an interview published on March 1, 2024, Ayesha admitted, “I was really stubborn in my earlier pregnancies. And that hurt me in the end. It made things really hard on me.” She then explained the lesson those experiences had taught her: “I had to learn to put my pride aside and realize it was okay to take help, to have people around me help and to not shy away from it.”That was not just about pregnancy. Ayesha had started thinking differently about motherhood as a whole. She explained that she could not do everything alone and said, “I know I can’t do this alone, it truly takes a village.”She also spoke about how that village keeps changing. “There’s always people coming in, people leaving, and people here forever. And that’s okay,” Ayesha said in 2024.That is where her story becomes more than a celebrity pregnancy story. Ayesha went through severe sickness, five hospital stays, childbirth and surgery, but she did not come away believing that strength meant carrying every burden herself.Instead, she learned to accept support.As for Ayesha, that may have been the biggest lesson of all. A mother can be strong while admitting she needs help. In fact, sometimes that honesty is exactly where her strength begins.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown’s Nigeria boxing appearance creates 76ers contract concerns after unexpected “I did 0 prep” admission
articles.summary: NBA News: Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown has drawn attention after a video showed him boxing in Nigeria during the offseason. Combat sports account Happy .
articles.body: Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown has drawn attention after a video showed him boxing in Nigeria during the offseason. Combat sports account Happy Punch shared the footage on September 10, showing Brown wearing gloves and headgear in a ring, along with clips of his training and basketball career. The post also included Brown’s comment: “I did 0 prep for this.” Brown was traded from the Boston Celtics to the 76ers in July.Jaylen Brown’s Nigeria boxing video and 7uice Foundation tripThe footage shows Brown inside a ring in Lagos in front of a crowd. He is seen wearing boxing gloves and headgear while facing an opponent, although details about the other person, the format of the event and whether it was a formal exhibition have not been reported.The video was shared by Happy Punch, which described the appearance as Brown’s boxing debut. However, Yardbarker noted that Brown had already taken part in a friendly boxing session in Morocco earlier this summer, so calling the Nigeria appearance his first time boxing would not give the full picture.Brown was in Nigeria as part of work connected to his 7uice Foundation. His foundation has focused on youth, education and community opportunities, and Brown has continued that work while preparing for his first season in Philadelphia. The Nigeria trip included meetings and community activities before the boxing footage surfaced.What caught many fans’ attention was Brown’s own comment about the lack of preparation. “I did 0 prep for this,” he wrote alongside the video. That line became a major part of the reaction because Brown is not only a professional basketball player but also one of the NBA’s highest-paid stars.Brown’s move to Philadelphia was one of the biggest NBA trades of the summer. The 76ers acquired him from Boston in exchange for Paul George and draft picks. NBA.com confirmed the trade on July 6. Brown had spent his entire first 10 NBA seasons with the Celtics, winning the 2024 NBA championship and Finals MVP award during that run.Jaylen Brown’s boxing family and 76ers contract concernsBoxing is familiar territory in Brown’s family. His father, Quenton Marselles Brown, known as Marselles Brown, was a professional heavyweight boxer who finished his career with a 33-18-1 record and won the World Boxing Union heavyweight title in 2016. Brown’s grandfather, Willie Brown, also had a professional boxing background.Jaylen Brown has also been open about his own interest in combat sports. He trains in Muay Thai and has spoken about possibly trying boxing or UFC after his basketball career. In February, he said he had discussed the idea with UFC CEO Dana White and would like to explore combat sports at some point.For now, though, Brown remains focused on basketball. That is why the Nigeria footage has raised questions about the risks of boxing while he is under contract with Philadelphia.Yardbarker reported that the standard NBA player contract includes a clause covering activities that carry a serious risk of injury, with boxing specifically listed among the activities that can require team permission. Neither Brown nor the 76ers had publicly commented on the Nigeria video when the report was published.The timing also matters. Brown is entering his first season with Philadelphia, and the 76ers will expect him to be ready for the new campaign. The Nigeria video does not show an injury, but it has still given fans another reason to question how much risk Brown should take during an important offseason.For now, the clearest facts are simple: Brown boxed in Nigeria, he said he had done no preparation for it, and the exact details of the event have not been made public.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Team USA coach Kara Lawson speaks out on prognosticators after dominant FIBA World Cup win over Hungary
articles.summary: Kara Lawson dismissed FIBA's power rankings after Team USA women's basketball demolished Hungary 108-56 in the World Cup quarterfinal match.
articles.body: Team USA women’s basketball coach Kara Lawson dismissed outside opinions after the Americans routed Hungary 108-56 in the FIBA Women’s World Cup quarterfinal Thursday. During the postgame press conference, Lawson was asked if a recent power ranking provided her team with any added motivation entering the final stage of the tournament. Lawson admitted she did not know about the ranking, but addressed those who may have more confidence in France, which appeared to be the more dominant team during group play. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "This is a big tournament, this is the World Cup, and it’s okay for people to have opinions on who they think is going to win and who they think is going to lose and who they’re cheering for and who they’re going to boo. That’s a competition, I think that’s why we love sport, it’s why it’s so exciting," Lawson said. "And now in this moment in women’s basketball you have more people than ever before that are giving their opinions and they’re making rankings and they’re doing that. That’s all great, we clearly don’t talk about any of that inside our bubble, and we really just focus on what we need to do. ITALY WOMEN'S BASKETBALL STAR TEARS INTO REF AFTER MISSING GAME-TYING SHOT VS US IN WOMEN'S WORLD CUP "Worrying about someone else’s opinion doesn’t serve you, because it doesn’t change whether you can do it or not. It’s just someone’s opinion." FIBA moved France ahead of the United States in its final "Smart Power Rankings" following the group stage. The Americans fell to second after narrowly escaping Italy with a 55-52 victory, their lowest-scoring World Cup performance since the introduction of the 3-point line in 1984. CAITLIN CLARK AND ANGEL REESE MUST NOW WORK TOGETHER AT WOMEN'S WORLD CUP AS WNBA TAKES A HIGH-STAKES BREAK The ranking also described the Americans’ on-court connections as a "work in progress." However, FIBA included a disclaimer stating that its rankings were "entirely subjective" and did not constitute an accurate ranking system. "As far as France, what a wonderful team, and they’ve had an outstanding World Cup so far, so they should have a lot of people thinking they can do well," Lawson said. France strengthened its case Thursday with a 90-61 quarterfinal victory over China. The French remain on the opposite side of the bracket, meaning they could only face the United States in the championship game. One of the biggest factors affecting the outlook for Lawson’s team entering the knockout stage was concern over the starting lineup. Lawson did not directly address that debate following Thursday’s victory. WNBA LEGEND BREANNA STEWART OPENS UP ON REPRESENTING AMERICA AT FIBA WOMEN'S WORLD CUP Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese once again came off the bench against Hungary. Lawson instead started Chelsea Gray, Jackie Young, Kahleah Copper, Napheesa Collier and Breanna Stewart. Lawson's commitment to keeping her veteran starting lineup has drawn frustration from fans, especially on Wednesday after Lawson suggested to OutKick that she will be keeping the veteran lineup going into the final stage. Still, the lineup worked against Hungary with obvious results. The U.S. scored 36 points in the opening quarter and carried a 59-30 advantage into halftime. The Americans shot 59% from the field, made 12 of their 23 3-point attempts and recorded 31 assists on 40 baskets. Their 108 points were the most ever scored in a Women’s World Cup quarterfinal, while they became the first team to record at least 30 assists at that stage of the tournament, according to FIBA. Collier led the Americans with 19 points and six rebounds. Every player on the U.S. roster scored, and five finished in double figures. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Clark narrowly missed her second double-double of the tournament, recording 10 points and a game-high nine assists in 20 minutes. Reese contributed nine points, six rebounds and three assists, while Bueckers added seven points and three assists. The victory also extended the Americans’ World Cup winning streak to 34 games. The program has not lost in the tournament since falling to Russia in the 2006 semifinals. The U.S. will face the winner of Thursday’s quarterfinal between Australia and Spain in Saturday’s semifinal. Lawson’s team is now two victories away from securing a fifth consecutive World Cup championship.

articles.title: Project B league signs more WNBA players, surpassing 20-name milestone
articles.summary: More WNBA players have signed to Project B as the basketball league grows. Here's who's on board.
articles.body:
Project B is slowly unveiling more WNBA names for the league's inaugural season, which starts in January 2027.

On Thursday, the global basketball organization announced six more athletes who plan to play. The latest wave includes 2024 WNBA champion Betnijah Laney-Hamilton and the No. 9 pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft Angela Dugalić ( Washington Mystics ), four-time all-star Brionna Jones ( Atlanta Dream ) and former Florida State standout Makayla Timpson ( Indiana Fever ). The list also includes two-time FIBA Women's EuroBasket champion Antonia Delaere ( Minnesota Lynx) and two-time Olympic medalist Valériane Ayayi ( Phoenix Mercury ).

"I've always believed in competing with purpose and being part of something bigger than yourself," Laney-Hamilton said in a release. "What excites me about Project B is the chance to compete with some of the best players from around the world while also having a real voice in what we're building. It's an opportunity to help shape something new for the game, and I'm excited to be part of it from the beginning."

2026 WNBA season is underway. See photos from the league's 30th year

The six bring Project B's list of WNBA players to 22 as the league approaches training camp in Seoul, Korea, from Jan. 6-12, 2027.

Other WNBA players who have signed with Project B include Azzi Fudd and Alanna Smith of the Dallas Wings , Alyssa Thomas of the Mercury, Awa Fam of the Seattle Storm , Jewell Loyd of the Las Vegas Aces , Jonquel Jones of the New York Liberty , Kamilla Cardoso of the Chicago Sky , Nneka Ogwumike of the Los Angeles Sparks and Kelsey Mitchell and Sophie Cunningham of the Fever.

"Project B is bringing together incredible players from around the world and creating something that gives us a real opportunity to help shape what comes next," Jones said. "I'm excited by the level of competition, but also by the chance for players to have a meaningful voice and stake in what we're building. I'm looking forward to being part of it from the beginning."

The concept for Project B is to have two separate leagues ― men and women ― with six teams, each with 11 players. Those teams will compete in a global circuit slated to kick off in Jan. 2027 and run through April 2027. Each city will host a 10-day event, crowning a city champion, and those victories will count towards a season-long championship. To date, Project B has revealed it will play in Tokyo, Japan and Valencia, Spain.

Every athlete who plays in Project B is expected to have equity in the league. Project B hasn't disclosed any salaries yet, but a league spokesperson previously told USA TODAY Sports they are "higher than anything you've ever seen in women's sports."

Project B has a host of investors in the league, including women's basketball legends Cheryl Miller, Candace Parker and Lauren Jackson and NFL Hall of Fame quarterback Steve Young. Additionally, the league has secured Host Broadcast Services (HBS) to be the official broadcaster for the league's inaugural circuit . HBS has broadcast the FIFA World Cup since 2002. The games will stream live on YouTube.

articles.title: USA and France ease into women's Basketball World Cup semis
articles.summary: The United States breezed into the semi-finals of the Women's Basketball World Cup with a commanding 108-56 win against Hungary on Thursday.The Americans and...
articles.body:
The United States breezed into the semi-finals of the Women's Basketball World Cup with a commanding 108-56 win against Hungary on Thursday.

Napheesa Collier topscored with 19 points while Caitlin Clark delivered nine assists and added 10 points in a dominant quarter-final performance in Berlin from the nation seeking a fifth consecutive title.

The Americans and their roster packed with WNBA stars will face either Spain or Australia in the semi-finals on Saturday and they remain on course to play the team they beat in the 2024 Olympic final, France, in the gold medal game.

Having survived a scare from Italy, who pushed them all the way in their second pool game before the Americans won 55-52, the USA have gone from strength to strength in the tournament in Germany.

On Thursday they raced into a 36-12 lead in the first quarter, effectively ending the game as a contest.

France comfortably beat China 90-61 in the day's second quarter-final to move into the last four.

WNBA star Xu Han led all scorers with 21 points, but her contribution was not enough for the Chinese to contend with a superior French team.

Zhang Ziyu, China's towering 2.23 metre (7ft 4in) teenage centre, played 18 minutes and scored seven points, but at 19 she has shown in this tournament that she has a bright future.

Janelle Salaun and Marine Johannes both scored 15 points for France and US-born Gabby Williams added 14 points.

The French will meet Germany in the semi-finals after the host nation defeated Belgium 93-74, despite a 29-point performance from Belgian power forward Emma Meesseman.

articles.title: UConn gets commitment from 5-star point guard NaVorro Bowman Jr., son of former All-Pro 49ers linebacker
articles.summary: Bowman is the first five-star recruit of the Class of 2027 to commit and the fourth landed during Dan Hurley's tenure in Storrs.
articles.body:
UConn landed a commitment from point guard NaVorro Bowman Jr., the son of All-Pro NFL linebacker NaVorro Bowman, ESPN's Adam Schefter reports .

A five-star recruit out of Notre Dame High School in Sherman Oaks, California, Bowman is rated by Rivals as the No. 5 point guard nationally and the No. 11 player overall . The 6-foot-3 guard is the only five-star player in the Class of 2027 to commit thus far.

As a junior, Bowman averaged 22.5 points and 5.0 assists while shooting 34% on 3-pointers in 29 games. On the Nike EYBL circuit this summer, he scored 20.5 points with 3.6 assists per game.

For UConn head coach Dan Hurley, Bowman is his first commitment for 2027 and the fourth five-star recruit that the two-time national championship coach has procured. Those include Braylon Mullins (2025), Liam McNeeley (2024) and 2025 NBA Rookie of the Year Stephon Castle (2023).

Hurley has also landed two four-star recruits in the class of 2026 with shooting guard Colben Landrew and point guard Junior County.

NaVorro Bowman Sr. played seven seasons in the NFL with the San Francisco 49ers and the then-Oakland Raiders. He was a four-time first-team All-Pro selection and three-time Pro Bowler.

His best season was in 2015 when he totaled 154 tackles (116 solo) with 7 tackles for loss, 1 fumble recovery and 2 passes defended. That was after missing the entire 2014 season with a torn ACL and MCL in his knee.

The 2025-26 national championship runner-up to Michigan, UConn is projected as a top 10 team to begin the 2026-27 campaign with Mullins and Silas Demary Jr. returning. However, Solo Ball will miss the entire season after undergoing surgery on his left wrist.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark, Angel Reese show unity for Team USA at World Cup amid tense history
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese connected repeatedly as Team USA set a Women's World Cup quarterfinal scoring record in a dominant win over Hungary.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese had their best game together as teammates on Thursday in the quarterfinal round of the FIBA Women's World Cup against Hungary. Their connection helped lead a historic 108-56 win for Team USA. It also gave fans another look at the growing partnership between two stars whose careers have been defined by competing against each other. Clark and Reese repeatedly connected during the victory. Clark finished with 10 points, nine assists, three rebounds and two steals. Reese added nine points, six rebounds, three assists, two steals and a block. Reese said their long history as opponents has made playing together easier. "Yeah, I mean, we’ve played against each other so many times. So I’m sure we know each other’s game. Like the back of each other’s hand. So I just easily dished it off to her. She dished it off to me. She knows my slides. I kind of got one to her today or maybe two. So it’s fun. We just continue to build chemistry because we know we’re going to be USA teammates for a while," Reese said in an interview with TNT after the game. CAITLIN CLARK AND ANGEL REESE MUST NOW WORK TOGETHER AT WOMEN'S WORLD CUP AS WNBA TAKES A HIGH-STAKES BREAK Both players came off the bench again Thursday, but their shared minutes gave Team USA a combination it may rely on throughout the rest of the tournament. Clark creates scoring opportunities with her passing and outside shooting. Reese provides rebounding, physical defense and pressure around the basket. While they were on the bench together, they were seen talking and laughing in a now-viral clip. Their partnership has developed despite a history that has fueled one of the most intense debates in American sports. The two stars first became permanently linked during the 2023 NCAA championship game. Reese led LSU to a 102-85 victory over Clark and Iowa before directing a "you can’t see me" gesture at Clark and pointing toward her ring finger late in the game. The moment sparked a national argument about sportsmanship, race and perceived double standards. Clark had used a similar gesture earlier in the NCAA Tournament, and she later defended Reese against the criticism she received. ANGEL REESE AND CAITLIN CLARK EXCHANGE WORDS IN SECOND DREAM-FEVER MEETING IN THREE DAYS Their rematch in the 2024 Elite Eight became one of the most anticipated games in women’s college basketball history. Clark produced 41 points and 12 assists as Iowa defeated LSU 94–87. Reese finished with 17 points and 20 rebounds before fouling out. The rivalry followed them into the WNBA after the Indiana Fever selected Clark first overall and the Chicago Sky drafted Reese seventh in 2024. Clark ultimately won the league’s Rookie of the Year award. Reese led the WNBA in rebounding and joined Clark on the All-Rookie team. The constant comparisons between their performances kept the rivalry at the center of the league’s rapid rise in attention. Their professional matchups also produced tense moments. Reese received a flagrant foul after striking Clark in the head during a 2024 game. In the opening game of the 2025 season, Clark received a flagrant foul for knocking Reese to the floor as Reese attempted to score. Reese quickly confronted Clark before teammates separated them. Both players said the latter incident was simply a basketball play. They have also repeatedly rejected the suggestion that their competition amounts to a personal feud. They previously showed they could play together during the 2024 WNBA All-Star Game. Clark assisted Reese on a layup as Team WNBA defeated the U.S. Olympic team. Clark finished with 10 assists, while Reese recorded 12 points and 11 rebounds. THE PREDOMINANT BASKETBALL DYNASTY ON EARTH IS AT STAKE AS AMERICA'S EYES TURN TO CAITLIN CLARK'S ROLE Their World Cup partnership carries significantly higher stakes. Neither player made the American roster for the 2024 Paris Olympics. The World Cup represents their first senior international tournament and an opportunity to establish themselves as part of the program’s future before the 2028 Los Angeles Games. Clark publicly praised Reese before the quarterfinal, calling her a fiery competitor with one of the strongest motors in the WNBA. "We're both fiery, fiery competitors and we want to win and it's one of the things I really admire about [Reese's] game," Clark told the Associated Press. "She's competitive and she has a tremendous motor, like she has one of the best motors in the league. She works just as hard as anybody on the court. So, it's been fun to be able to play with her." That competitive energy helped fuel a historic performance Thursday. The Americans scored 36 points in the opening quarter and took a 59–30 advantage into halftime. Team USA shot 59% from the field and recorded 31 assists on 40 baskets. Its 108 points were the most ever scored in a Women’s World Cup quarterfinal. The victory extended the United States’ World Cup winning streak to 34 games and moved the team within two victories of a fifth consecutive championship. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Team USA will face the winner of Australia and Spain in Saturday’s semifinal. Clark and Reese will enter that game with the same goal and, for one of the few times in their careers, the same fans behind them.

articles.title: Jonathan Kuminga Says He Wanted 'Winning Culture' After Snubbing Lakers to Sign with T-Wolves
articles.summary: Veteran forward Jonathan Kuminga cited the Minnesota Timberwolves' "winning culture" as a decisive factor in his decision to sign with the team.
articles.body:
Veteran forward Jonathan Kuminga cited the Minnesota Timberwolves' "winning culture" as a decisive factor in his decision to sign with the team.

During his introductory press conference Thursday, he said the Wolves had the "best winning culture I could've chosen out of the options."

ESPN's Anthony Slater and Shams Charania reported the 23-year-old had other offers from the Los Angeles Lakers, Chicago Bulls and Portland Trail Blazers. The Lakers were willing to pay him around $12 million annually on a three-year deal, which matches the entire total of his two-year pact with Minnesota.

Historically, the on-court success of the Timberwolves pales in comparison to that of Los Angeles. Heading into the 2026-27 season, they're basically on equal footing. Minnesota can also point to reaching the Western Conference Finals more recently than L.A.

Right now, the Wolves might have fewer question marks in terms of their roster. Acquiring LaMelo Ball was a big shakeup to the status quo, but the Lakers lost LeBron James and hedged a lot of their future on Walker Kessler, who has logged 201 appearances through his first four years.

One could argue Minnesota is better positioned to contend.

As much as Kuminga weighed what he thought the "culture" of each franchise was, the finances played a role in his free agency, too. He's clearly happy to bet on himself for one year with an eye toward next summer:

If Kuminga plays well in Minnesota, he can opt out and return to free agency after a season. He wouldn't have had that kind of flexibility by taking a multiyear contract from the Lakers.

articles.title: NBA mailbag: Are the Celtics still a title contender? Which teams are flying under the radar?
articles.summary: We answer some of your NBA questions with the 2026-27 season right around the corner.
articles.body:
After what has felt like the longest offseason in recent memory, the 2026-27 NBA season is right around the corner. In less than three weeks, all 30 teams will answer wide-ranging questions about their summer business and future expectations.

But why wait? Thanks to those of you who sent in inquiries of your own, let's get to it.

Are the Celtics still an NBA title contender after losing Jaylen Brown ? — @thomasnoble12

Yes, and more folks should be talking about this.

Do I think that the 56-win Celtics, after losing Brown to the rival 76ers , can replicate a similar model without one of the league's top-15ish players? Probably not.

Am I signing up for Mazzulla ball with an older, wiser Paul George (40% outside shooter on nearly seven attempts per game) bringing an efficient blend of creation, spacing and defensive versatility, Mitchell Robinson 's possession-extending activity and Mike Conley 's veteran savvy — with a healthy Jayson Tatum ? Absolutely.

What Boston can achieve this season is juxtaposed with the very loud and proud Knicks reign in the Eastern Conference, the sole reason why a plethora of contenders have beefed up over the past few months. But why shouldn't the Celtics be considered among the favorites? Excellent coaching? Check. Heliocentric, healthy talent? Check. Reliable second fiddle that can create for others and himself? Check. Elite floor spacing? Check. Rim protection and offensive rebounding? Check.

What team/teams do you think are flying under the radar as the season approaches? — @qschneid14

I'll simplify my choices here, but "under the radar" to me implies that Team X is actually better than the consensus or isn't being discussed with the same breadth as their contemporaries. A few stick out:

Atlanta Hawks : CJ McCollum was shoehorned into a pseudo-lead ball-handler role he wasn't necessarily equipped for (and got absolutely battered in the postseason). I appreciate the front office synthesizing their playmaking woes and bringing in underrated operators in Ryan Nembhard and Devin Carter , as well as drafting Houston 's Kingston Flemings. I've also long beaten the drum of teams siphoning off talent from perennial winning organizations, and acquiring both Lu Dort and Aaron Wiggins from the Oklahoma City Thunder should pay immediate dividends at both ends of the floor.

Los Angeles Clippers : The fallout from the Kawhi Leonard/Aspiration investigation is tremendous, embarrassing and unfortunate, so can you legally qualify as under the radar if the whole country is talking about you? Perhaps from an actual basketball perspective, where I have the Clippers projected to clear their 28.5 expected win total by some distance. I recently wrote about what their on-court product for 2026-27 could look like and believe there's a path to productivity, albeit with underground expectations.

Utah Jazz : Losing Walker Kessler and his rim protection stings quite a bit, but Jaren Jackson Jr.'s frontcourt versatility paired with Lauri Markkanen 's floor spacing gives them an edge in a loaded Western Conference. The electric duo of Darryn Peterson and Keyonte George will make most of the headlines and League Pass rankings, but veteran wing Josh Okogie is the swing play here. He's a top-50 defensive impact player, per DARKO, a decent enough shooter and runner to provide offensive value despite his shortcomings, and one of the harder workers you'll see.

How far do you have the Miami Heat going? — @sosaaa_behbie

Vegas is projecting the Heat to win 45.5 games, which sounds like a borderline play-in team. Ironically enough, I think Miami could get to 50 if it was in the opposite conference (what a time we're living in), but anywhere from 46-48 games sounds like the sweet spot for this group.

I fully expect the Heat to finish the season as a top-five defensive unit. There is no better, more physical or versatile frontcourt pairing than Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo . (We're not even throwing the ever-eager Bobby Portis into the equation right now.) Klay Thompson and Tim Hardaway Jr. should improve on the Heat's low shooting volume (20th in 3-point rate, 12th in conversion) and spacing issues that may arise.

Is that enough to seriously challenge in the East?

Miami has all the makings of a sixth, seventh or eighth seed you wouldn't want to see in a seven-game series, but there are too many offensive questions raised to give the Heat much of a shot outside of a shocker first-round emergence. Is Davion Mitchell prepared for a spike in creation responsibility and scoring? Can Andrew Wiggins slot back into a diminished role with fewer touches and remain efficient? This is somewhat of a hastily put-together group tasked with contending immediately. I still think they're a few pieces away.

In your opinion, which team improved the most this offseason? — @MrEd315

The simple answer is Philly, right? You'd be hard-pressed to find an organization that fundamentally raised its chances of hoisting a Larry O'Brien more than the 76ers, who added Jaylen Brown and LeBron James to the ranks, along with supporting cast members like Dean Wade , Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope .

But I take it you didn't come here for the simple answer. So, I'll go with the Hornets. Let me explain.

To me, the team(s) that improved the most this offseason are the ones that established an identity in the previous campaign, retained some sort of flexibility and augmented how they play either offensively or defensively (or both in the perfect scenario).

In Charlotte, LaMelo Ball 's departure was the natural landmark event, but with him went a great deal of rim pressure, perimeter creation, gravity and, by proxy, 3-point proficiency. ( Miles Bridges also took a substantial amount of outside shots, but his waning efficiency won't be missed as much.)

Head coach Charles Lee has created an environment that relies on ball movement, relocation and a heavy perimeter onslaught (the Hornets finished second in 3-point attempt rate , third in conversion rate ).

Lee's approach is more egalitarian than heliocentric — which means more Coby White , less Ball — and he saw enough from the former's 21-game sample size to warrant such a bold decision. White, like Ball, handled the ball a ton, but his efficiency clears his predecessor's, his 85th-percentile assist rate suggests a bigger role, and the combination of volume and output paints a positive picture.

It's even more obvious looking at the incoming names ( Grayson Allen , Royce O'Neale, Naz Reid ) that Lee plans on keeping the Hornets — a team that finished 20th in passes made and 15th in assists — a 3-point juggernaut. He wants enough floor-spacers to keep defenses honest, understanding the gap in star quality between Ball and White (which affects how opposing defenses load up).

Here's what he now has at his disposal, according to NBA RAPM's true shooting spacing metric, which incorporates shots taken via spot-up opportunities, handoffs and actions off screens:

Allen: 92nd percentile true shooting attempts, 80th percentile true shooting %

O'Neale: 75th percentile true shooting attempts, 91st percentile true shooting %

Reid: 97th percentile true shooting attempts, 68th percentile true shooting %

Brandon Miller : 93rd percentile, 75th percentile

Kon Knueppel : 87th percentile, 92nd percentile

The Hornets know how they want to play and went out to maximize that potential. (O'Neale and Dorian Finney-Smith , with a full season of recovery under his belt, should also aid in their defensive efforts.) Add that to the trove of draft assets they picked up in the process — two first-rounders, three first-round swaps and six seconds — and it's hard to argue against their body of work.

articles.title: España toca el cielo y luchará por las medallas en el Mundial
articles.standfirst: Borda el juego ante Australia en una primera mitad de ensueño
articles.summary: Borda el juego ante Australia en una primera mitad de ensueño
articles.body: En un partido en el que por momentos llegó a bordar el baloncesto, España se metió de la manera más brillante posible en la lucha por las medallas del Mundial de baloncesto femenino. Lo hizo ganando a Australia 66-89 con un juego extraordinario con todas sus jugadoras aportando, con una gran defensa y un ataque demoledor. En el primer cuarto sumó 31 puntos. Al descanso ya ganaba por 21 con 58 puntos en su casillero. A este nivel, cabe preguntarse dónde está el límite de estas chicas. El rival del sábado es mayúsculo, Estados Unidos, pero tras ver al equipo de Méndez ante las oceánicas en su partido de cuartos, el vigente campeón del Mundo tiene mucho de qué preocuparse. Hay que recordar que en Australia faltaban Ezi Magbegor y Alanna Smith, que era como perder más de 25 puntos de media, y que tampoco jugó Jade Melbourne. Muchas e importantísimas bajas que trataron de cubrir Reid, con un comienzo sensacional (tres triples seguidos) y Talbot. Pero era la fiesta de España a la que se apuntaron todas las jugadoras de la selección. El primer gran arreón de España y, probablemente, el definitivo tuvo lugar al final del primer cuarto con tres minutos y medio de ensueño. De repente, del 13-15 se pasó al 15-29 (2-14 de parcial) y finalmente al 17-31 al final del acto. Iyana había mantenido al equipo en los primeros minutos, pero ese arreón perteneció a Alba Torrens, dos triples y sus primeros puntos del campeonato, y a Alicia Flórez, en estado de gracia. En el segundo cuarto la ventaja parecía esfumarse con un 8-2 australiano (25-33) al que respondió España con un 3-13 demoledor (28-46) cuando jugadoras como Gustafson, Conde o Cazorla dieron un paso adelante en el partido. En plena exhibición ofensiva construida desde la defensa, España llevaba 58 puntos al descanso (37-58), la segunda mejor anotación al descanso de la selección en un partido del Mundial. A ese nivel estaba jugando. Histórico. La anotación cayó en picado en la reanudación. España había anotado 31 y 27 puntos en los dos primeros cuartos. En el tercer acto, el parcial fue de 14-12. Pero lo importante es que las diferencias se conservaban, España ahorró algunos esfuerzos sin comprometer el resultado. El rival también intentó meterse en el partido. A esas alturas del partido, Megan Gustafson ya era la líder anotadora de la selección. Jugó un partido muy sólido en la pintura y acabó con 16 puntos y 7/11 en tiros. La máxima de 23 que tuvo España, 41-64, mediado el tercer cuarto se redujo a 14 (60-74) a falta de 7:26 para que expirara el partido y luego a 13 (63-76) tres minutos después. La defensa había blindado el resultado para las de Méndez a pesar de la pérdida de inspiración en ataque. España controlaba el partido y acabó ganando con mucha claridad. Tras Gustafson en materia anotadora, Iyana Martín hizo 13 (9 en el primer tramo con tres triples), María Conde firmó 10 puntos, y Alicia Flórez otros 10. España alcanzó uno de los grandes objetivos con los que vino al Mundial: luchar por las medallas. Pero todas y cada una de las jugadoras de la selección saben que el trabajo no está terminado. Queda mucho por hacer y por disfrutar.

articles.title: Former LSU center Kate Koval granted waiver by NCAA to enter transfer portal
articles.summary: Koval, born and raised in Ukraine, told LSU head coach Kim Mulkey she was leaving the program after a Russian player was added to the roster.
articles.body:
Former LSU center Kate Koval has been granted a waiver by the NCAA to enter the transfer portal. The junior will be immediately eligible to compete for her next school, according to several reports.

The 6-foot-5 Ukrainian native decided to leave the LSU program two weeks ago for what was announced as "personal reasons." Speculation followed that Koval's decision was spurred by LSU coach Kim Mulkey adding Russian center Anna Minaeva to the roster.

Koval confirmed that was her reason for leaving LSU in a social media post.

"At the conclusion of last season, I fully intended to return and continue my collegiate career at LSU," Koval wrote . "However, in April, several days after the transfer portal had closed, I was informed of the decision to sign a Russian player." "My father serves in the Ukrainian military and takes tremendous pride in defending his country against Russian aggression," she continued. "For me, this war is not distant or abstract. People close to me have been killed and wounded in Russian attacks, and places where I grew up and first began playing basketball have been destroyed by missile strikes."

"My father serves in the Ukrainian military and takes tremendous pride in defending his country against Russian aggression," she continued. "For me, this war is not distant or abstract. People close to me have been killed and wounded in Russian attacks, and places where I grew up and first began playing basketball have been destroyed by missile strikes."

Koval is being allowed to enter the transfer portal under a "legislative relief waiver," USA Today reports . Such a waiver is granted beyond a sport-specific transfer window due to an "exigent event outside the student-athlete's control unrelated to athletics opportunities or participation at their current institution that demands the student-athlete's immediate departure from the institution," according to The Athletic .

In her lone season at LSU, Koval averaged 8.3 points and 6.3 rebounds in 35 games (17 starts). She began her collegiate career at Notre Dame, transferring to LSU after her freshman season.

Mulkey told the New Orleans Advocate that she met with Koval about recruiting Minaeva and explained that she understood how Koval felt about Russia, but could not "make a decision to not recruit somebody that can help our program because of a conflict between two countries."

The LSU coach went on to say that she hoped the two players could become "ambassadors" amid the war between Ukraine and Russia, which began in 2022, and perhaps even help end the conflict. Koval responded skeptically. She announced her departure from LSU a week later.

articles.title: Jonathan Kuminga Reveals Why He Chose Timberwolves Over Lakers: “I Wanted A Winning Culture…”
articles.summary: Timberwolves forward Jonathan Kuminga explains the decision process for his 2026 free agency.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Hawks declined Jonathan Kuminga's $24.3 million team option, making him an unrestricted free agent for the first time in his career. While Kuminga initially struggled to secure the terms he was seeking, he eventually settled on a more agreeable arrangement, joining a well-stocked Minnesota Timberwolves team for two years and $13 million.

Despite a complicated history in the NBA, Kuminga had his fair share of suitors, including the Los Angeles Lakers , who were aggressive from the start . According to Kuminga, however, the Timberwolves have the "championship culture" he believes he's the perfect fit for.

"The process was up and down," said Kuminga in his introductory press conference . "Just looking back, I think I would say it's one of the best decisions I've made, just looking at the roster, looking at the young group of guys they have and just seeing what they've done in the past. I think I fit well with this culture… I think the choice was about trying to win, trying to help them win, and that's why I made this decision."

Despite their recent success, the Timberwolves have never actually won the NBA championship, calling into question Kuminga's claims about their "championship culture." Some fans took it as a direct diss toward the Lakers, who have long been among the most accomplished franchises in the league. They were willing to offer Kuminga more money, as well as a starting role.

Nevertheless, Kuminga weighed all his options and only came to a decision after much thought and deliberation with friends and family. He also spoke with Timberwolves players and coaches directly, confirming suspicions that he would fit well with their overall vibe . In the end, that was all he needed to make his pick.

"I prayed over this and asked God to guide me and give me the best decision," Kuminga added . "I think this was the best decision for me. I wanted to go to a winning culture, and I think this was one of the best winning cultures I could have chosen out of all the options. As I said earlier, I spoke to so many people on this team, including the front office, coaches, and some of the players, and it was just the vibe I was looking for. I think that made this decision way easier, and I went with it."

Kuminga's signing was another massive win for the Timberwolves, who had just added LaMelo Ball to play with Anthony Edwards , Rudy Gobert , and Jaden McDaniels . Together, they can challenge the NBA's most elite teams and bring glory to a franchise that has only known disappointment. Clearly, in the eyes of players and fans, the Wolves are in an overall better place than the Lakers (and most teams in the West), and have a core that can compete for many years to come.

For Kuminga, this is an opportunity to prove his worth and s how that he can play a big role on a contending team . With averages of 12.2 points, 5.6 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 0.6 steals, and 0.3 blocks per game on 46.3% shooting last season, he has shown glimpses of greatness, but he now has all the tools to expand his game and reach the heights of NBA success. Best of all, if it all goes wrong, he still has some level of control over his future, thanks to his $6.3 million player option in 2027-28.

articles.title: New Cruise Coach Steve Scalzi Sees ‘One NBA Ecosystem’
articles.summary: Detroit's new G League head coach laid out how he sees the Pistons pipeline. #Pistons
articles.body:
Hired from within the building, Motor City Cruise head coach Steve Scalzi understands the job ahead: win games, and develop players who can be called up to the NBA. In his introductory press conference Thursday afternoon, Scalzi acknowledged that reality. He also recognizes he is stepping into a program that has already succeeded at both.

Asked how success with the Cruise translates to success for the Pistons , Scalzi said he views it all as "one NBA ecosystem."

"I like to think of every last player on the roster as NBA-ready or NBA potential in an NBA building every day. So why are they not already NBA players? Why are we not all already NBA staffers? I like to think of us as all the same (and at the) same level to an extent."

That correlation leaks into every facet of the foundation, as he explained: "Aside from just physically sharing an environment here, we share a mindset in our alignment. Our meetings prove as such, and then I think the success and the fact that you're really able to (develop and win) at the same time in this environment."

Scalzi has been an assistant coach with the Pistons since 2023, so he has seen the organization at its highs and its lows. He has also been part of a program that developed players and won at the same time. "That's a bit challenging in the NBA, and we're super proud of it; to do more of that at the G League level is the challenge that's ahead of me."

Steve Scalzi Points to Players Already in the Building

With more than a decade of coaching experience across the NBA and G League, Scalzi has crossed paths with some true greats. Kevin Durant and Russell Westbrook in Oklahoma City , to name a couple. Yet when it comes to naming the kind of player he wants, he doesn't have to look outside the locker room.

"The players that I enjoy most are the ones whose improvement rate over time is really, really drastic. I think about the progress of the people who made this Cruise program what it is, whether it's Daniss Jenkins or Wendell Moore , or Tolu Smith , or John Ukomadu, Chaz Lanier ; (incoming players) are gonna get a lot of film with those guys to understand how they can impact and continue to make baby steps when they first step on the floor in the Pistons environment, then before you know it, they're calling that place home every single night."

Scalzi is taking over in place of Jamelle McMillan, who is expected to join the Chicago Bulls . During McMillan's three seasons with the Cruise, multiple players were called up or converted to standard NBA contracts , including Daniss Jenkins and Tolu Smith. Last season, McMillan led the franchise to its first playoff win , a 120-105 victory over Raptors 905. The standard has been set, and set high.

Scalzi begins his quest to carry that standard forward on Nov. 10, when the Cruise open on the road against the Cleveland Charge.

articles.title: Willy manda en el estreno del Unicaja en el Costa del Sol
articles.standfirst: Los malagueños ganan a La Laguna Tenerife (80-76) y esperan al Real Madrid este sábado
articles.summary: Los malagueños ganan a La Laguna Tenerife (80-76) y esperan al Real Madrid este sábado
articles.body: El Unicaja se llevó ante La Laguna Tenerife el primer partido del Trofeo Costa del Sol en su XV edición. El equipo de Txus Vidorreta tuvo el partido controlado durante muchos minutos, llegó a dominar por 16 puntos y terminó necesitando una aparición estelar de su pívot para cerrar la victoria ante La Laguna Tenerife (80-76). Los canarios llegaron a ponerse por delante en el último cuarto, pero Hernangómez apareció cuando más apretaba el marcador. Terminó con 16 puntos, 11 rebotes y 32 de valoración. El Tenerife salió mejor. Un 0-5 de inicio obligó al Unicaja a reaccionar. Y lo hizo de inmediato. Brazdeikis rompió la sequía con un mate en transición y abrió la puerta a un parcial de 10-0. El equipo malagueño empezó a mover el balón con criterio y encontró acierto desde fuera. La renta no dejó de crecer hasta alcanzar el 24-11 al final del primer cuarto. El segundo acto mantuvo la misma dinámica. El Unicaja alcanzó el 30-14 y parecía tener el encuentro bajo control. Guy trató de despertar al Tenerife, pero Perry y Cameron Hunt respondieron. También Alberto Díaz y Willy Hernangómez comenzaron a entenderse a la perfección en el bloqueo directo. El 38-22 reflejaba el dominio malagueño. Pero el Tenerife no se rindió. Shermadini empezó a encontrar espacios y los visitantes recortaron diferencias con un parcial de 4-10. El Unicaja perdió algo de fluidez y llegó al descanso con una ventaja todavía importante, pero ya lejos de la máxima: 42-32. La reacción canaria continuó tras el paso por vestuarios. Hunt y Noua intentaron estirar de nuevo la ventaja, aunque Guy y Huertas contestaron cada golpe. El Unicaja seguía por delante (54-43), pero el partido había cambiado. Tenerife encontraba más fácilmente el aro y amenazaba con completar la remontada. Entonces apareció Lukosius. Dos triples consecutivos dieron aire a los de Vidorreta y devolvieron la diferencia a los once puntos (62-51). La respuesta aurinegra fue inmediata. Dos acciones de 2+1 colocaron el 62-57. Y ahí apareció Willy. El pívot se hizo dueño de la zona. Reboteó. Anotó. Aguantó al Unicaja cuando más lo necesitaba. Lukosius volvió a castigar desde fuera y los malagueños recuperaron los diez puntos de margen (67-57). Bamba, desde el triple, dejó el partido abierto antes del último cuarto: 67-60. Jaime Fernández puso al Tenerife a solo tres puntos con un triple. El Unicaja se atascó y acumuló varias faltas en ataque. Los visitantes olieron sangre. Bamba convirtió otro 2+1 y puso el 69-67. Poco después, el propio jugador tinerfeño clavó un triple. Por primera vez en el tramo decisivo, el Tenerife estaba por delante: 69-70 con 4:23 por jugar. El partido entró en el intercambio de golpes. Canasta de Willy. Respuesta de Hunter. Otra de Willy. Y empate a 74. Ahí se acabó el margen de error. Hernangómez asumió la responsabilidad. Primero, desde la línea de tiros libres. Después, al poste. Dos acciones que devolvieron el mando al Unicaja (77-74). El Tenerife buscó la respuesta, pero Perry recuperó un balón y Hunt castigó desde el perímetro a falta de 41 segundos. El triple puso el 80-74 y dejó el triunfo prácticamente sentenciado. López-Arostegui anotó bajo el aro para poner el definitivo 80-76. No hubo tiempo para más. El Unicaja cerró su estreno en el XV Torneo Costa del Sol con una victoria trabajada y con una certeza: cuando el partido se puso cuesta arriba, Willy Hernangómez apareció para marcar la diferencia. 80- Unicaja (24+18+25+13): Perry (12), Pantzar (5), Brazdeikis (7), Barreiro (5), Kravish (3) -quinteto inicial- Lukosius (9), Djedovic (0), Tyson Pérez (0), Hunt (13), Díaz (3), Noua (7), Hernángomez (16). 76- Tenerife (11+21+28+16): Fitipaldo (0), Guy (12), López-Arostegui (4), Doornekamp (0), Hunter (12) -quinteto inicial- Huertas (8), Shermadini (17), Bamba (14), Van Beck (2), Abromaitis (2), Fernández (5), Alderete (0). articles.body: El Barça se impuso con claridad al MoraBanc Andorra en un encuentro que dominó durante los cuarenta minutos gracias al acierto en el triple (88-84). A pesar de las bajas de Yoan Moakoundou y Tosan Evbuomwan por lesión, y de Kevin Punter por gestión de cargas, los de Aleksander Sekulic llevaron la iniciativa desde el primer cuarto y supieron resistir al intento de remontada rival en el tercer cuarto, especialmente gracias a Darío Brizuela (19 puntos y 20 de valoración). Kyle Kuric (21 puntos y 24 de valoración) fue el mejor para los andorranos. De este modo, el equipo azulgrana se jugará su pase a final mañana ante el Kids&Us Manresa (21:00 horas). El ganador del partido se enfrentará al iLerna Lleida el domingo a las 12:00 horas. El encuentro se inició en un breve intercambio de canastas entre ambos equipos. Mientras que el conjunto del principado se impuso en la pintura, el Barça basó su juego en el tiro exterior y las transiciones, y logró situar una renta de seis puntos (12-6, min .5). A pesar de que Zan Tabak pidió tiempo muerto, el acierto blaugrana desde el perímetro no disminuyó y, con una gran defensa, los locales consiguieron ampliar la ventaja hasta el final del cuatro (28-16, min.10). En el segundo período, el cuadro del principado reaccionó con un parcial 4-12 de salida que rebajó la diferencia a cuatro puntos. En un tramo comprometido para los de Aleksander Sekulic, Justin Robinson cogió las rendas de su equipo y lo mantuvo por delante en el marcador (37-32, min.15). Por su parte, el Andorra no logró mantener la intensidad y el acierto durante todo el cuarto, y vieron como el Barça los castigó elevando nuevamente la ventaja por encima de los dos dígitos, lo que obligó a Tabak a parar el choque (44-34, min.18). El parón no surtió efecto para el conjunto del Pirineo. Ello lo aprovecharon los blaugranas para establecer una nueva máxima ventaja antes del paso por vestuarios mediante un triple de Darío Brizuela (52-37, min.20). Tras el descanso, ambos conjuntos libraron un intercambio de golpes que benefició a los del principado, que volvieron a situarse a ocho tantos (56-48, min.24). La diferencia se estabilizó durante varios minutos. No obstante, cuando parecía que el Barça controlaba el ritmo del partido, los visitantes anotaron el 69-64 que provocó que Sekulic pidiera tiempo muerto. El choque se fue al último asalto tras dos tiros libres de Wesley Iwundu (69-66, min.30). En el cuarto período, los locales despejaron cualquier duda con un parcial 7-2 en dos minutos que abrió una pequeña brecha en el marcador. Esta vez los de Zan Tabak no fueron capaces de ofrecer réplica ante un Barça que, al no acumular faltas, subió un punto la agresividad defensiva (81-71, min.36). En los últimos instantes, los tricolores se situaron a cuatro puntos a falta de treinta segundos, pero los fallos de Kassius Robertson y Owen Aquino sentenciaron el partido a favor de los azulgranas (88-84, min.40). 88 – Barça: Umude (5), Robinson (11), Brizuela (15), Nebo (6), Parra (14) -cinco inicial- Gibson (9), Martin (16), Ubal (-), Nkamhoua (5), Núñez (-), Balcerowski (3) y Minaya (-). 84 - MoraBanc Andorra: McGriff (8), Luz (5), Robertson (6), Iwundu (11), Pustovyi (5) -cinco inicial- Mutic (9), Best (12), Ortega (2), Aquino (-), Kuric (21), Bottiroli (-) y Radosevic (5). articles.summary: El seleccionador destacó el concepto Equipo tras la victoria ante Australia
articles.body: España ganó de forma muy brillante a Australia en su partido de cuartos de final. Bordó el baloncesto en la primera parte y cuidó su ventaja en la segunda. Y compartió mucho el balón. De todo ello habló el seleccionador Miguel Méndez. “Estoy muy feliz. Honestamente hay que decir que han jugado con la baja de dos de sus mejores jugadoras, pero con este equipo ganaron el miércoles a Italia. Siguen siendo un gran equipo”. Sobre las 25 asistencias que dio España en el partido, su tope en el campeonato, Méndez dijo:“Eso es algo que forma parte de nuestro catecismo. Somos un equipo, con mayúsculas. Hoy en defensa todas se han ayudado y eso da confianza, pues en ataque tenemos que hacer lo mismo compartiendo el balón”. El seleccionador se refirió luego a Alicia Flórez, elegida mejor jugadora del partido: “No sé quién ha sido la máxima anotadora hoy (Megan Gustafson), pero el MVP se lo han dado a Alicia. Y en cada partido ha sido una, van cambiando porque hay un gran trabajo de todas. Es complicado decir quién ha destacado sobre el resto. Eso es algo en lo que venimos trabajando desde el año 21. Y el equipo cree en ello”. Méndez incidió en esa idea: “Si hoy hubieran elegido MVP a Awa, a Iyana, a Raquel, a María o el partidazo de Maite, no le hubiera sorprendido a nadie. A Alicia le hace especial ilusión”. El seleccionador habló de dónde está el techo de esta selección: “Ahora mismo la respuesta la tendremos entre el sábado y el domingo. Ante EEUU vamos a darlo todo. Prepararemos el partido lo mejor posible, lo prepararemos para ganar como siempre”. María Conde, destacada en el partido, habló de lo que viene: “Hay mucha ilusión, todas queríamos estar en esta situación cuando arrancó el campeonato”.

articles.title: Inspiring story on fatherhood:“That’s my main goal, to try and be a better father than the one I had”- How LeBron James turned pain into a promise
articles.summary: NBA News: At 19, LeBron James was already carrying the weight of an NBA franchise when fatherhood gave him an entirely different responsibility. His first son, .
articles.body: At 19, LeBron James was already carrying the weight of an NBA franchise when fatherhood gave him an entirely different responsibility. His first son, Bronny, was born in October 2004, just months after James entered the league as the No. 1 overall pick. More than two decades later, his early promise to become a better father still offers a revealing look at the man behind the basketball legend.LeBron James’ fatherhood began with a promiseThe quote that best captures LeBron James’ approach to fatherhood came at a defining moment in his young life. According to contemporary reports, James spoke to the Akron Beacon Journal around the time his first child was born in October 2004.His words were simple, but the reason behind them was deeply personal.“That’s my main goal, to try and be a better father than the one I had,” James told the newspaper. “I didn’t know him. I didn’t know the situation he was in. But I’m going to do my job the best way I can. I’m excited about it. It’s a wonderful opportunity in life.”James had grown up primarily with his mother, Gloria, without his biological father playing a meaningful role in his childhood. Becoming a father himself therefore meant more than welcoming a baby. It gave him a chance to build the kind of family relationship he had never experienced.The timing made the moment even more striking. James was only 19, preparing for his second NBA season and learning how to handle the expectations that came with being the league's most celebrated young player.His life was moving at an extraordinary pace. Basketball demanded nearly everything from him, yet fatherhood gave him a reason to think beyond the next game, season or championship.LeBron James learned fatherhood without a manualAs his family grew, James repeatedly acknowledged that parenting did not come with a perfect formula.In a 2017 Vogue interview, he explained that there was no definitive guide for raising children because every child and family situation was different. He also credited Savannah James with taking the lead at home while his NBA career kept him on the road.That reality became particularly important as James and Savannah raised Bronny, Bryce and Zhuri.Years earlier, James had made a similar point during a CNN interview with Rachel Nichols. Asked about guiding his children, he stressed that parents can provide values and direction, but ultimately children must learn to make their own decisions.His philosophy was not to dictate every move. It was to prepare his children for the moments when he would not be there to make the decision for them.That approach also shaped the way he viewed his sons' basketball careers. James knew better than most that having an NBA superstar as a father could create enormous expectations.In 2018, while discussing Bronny on The Shop, James admitted that he regretted giving his son his name because of the pressure that could follow him. He explained that his original motivation came from his own childhood and his desire to do things differently.“The only thing I can do is give them the blueprint, and it’s up to them to take their own course whenever that time comes.”That line reveals another important part of James' parenting style. He could offer experience, protection and advice, but he could not live his children's lives for them.LeBron James admits the NBA took time away from his childrenFor all the success James achieved, fatherhood also forced him to confront a painful cost of professional sports: time.After eventually sharing an NBA court with Bronny, James reflected on the years he had spent travelling and playing.“It’s family. It’s always been family over everything,” James said, acknowledging that his career had meant missing moments involving Bronny, Bryce and Zhuri.That admission adds another layer to his early promise.Being a better father was never simply about providing financially. James understood that being present mattered too. NBA seasons are long. Travel is constant. Even the most successful athlete cannot recover every birthday, school event or ordinary family evening lost to work.His comments over the years suggest that this tension has stayed with him.Yet basketball also produced moments that made the sacrifices feel worthwhile.When Bronny joined the Los Angeles Lakers, James became the first father to play alongside his son in an NBA regular-season game. The historic moment arrived on Oct. 22, 2024, when the two checked into the Lakers' game against the Minnesota Timberwolves.For James, the achievement carried an emotional meaning that went beyond basketball.The teenager who had once promised to become a better father than the one he had was now sharing an NBA floor with his own son.LeBron James’ children became part of his greatest achievementJames has never suggested that being a father is easy. Instead, his comments show how much he has learned while raising three children under extraordinary public attention.In 2016, he told ESPN that one of his favorite parts of fatherhood was watching his children grow and recognizing pieces of his younger self in them.That may be one of the most human parts of his story. The NBA superstar who spends his career being judged by statistics and championships also has to deal with the ordinary emotions of parenthood.He gets proud. He worries. He gives advice. He sometimes sees his younger self in his children.And he has had to learn when to step in and when to let them find their own way.That balance became even more meaningful after Bronny suffered cardiac arrest during a workout at USC in July 2023. James later said he would dedicate the following season to his son, adding, “Understanding that puts everything in perspective.”The episode reminded James and his family that careers, records and championships can suddenly become secondary.His fatherhood journey has therefore come full circle in a way that few could have predicted when he was 19. He entered adulthood without the relationship with his own father that many children take for granted. He then became a father himself while carrying the expectations of an entire basketball city.Instead of allowing that absence to define him, James turned it into a standard for himself.The exact viral quote about giving his children everything he did not have should not be attributed to him. His documented words are arguably more powerful anyway.“That’s my main goal, to try and be a better father than the one I had.”More than 20 years later, his career shows how seriously he took that promise.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham dropped a new podcast on Thursday, discussing star teammate Caitlin Clark, the WNBA's next commissioner and more.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham dropped a new podcast on Thursday, discussing star teammate Caitlin Clark, the WNBA's next commissioner and more.

WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert plans to retire at the end of the 2026 campaign, meaning the league will get a new commissioner as it continues to experience rapid growth.

Cunningham detailed what her first order of business would be if she were commissioner.

Caitlin Clark talks playing with Angel Reese

"The first thing I would do is make sure every team has a functional practice facility," Cunningham said (27-minute mark). "There are teams in the WNBA — we're the best league in the entire world — there are people practicing at, like, YMCAs... The tides are turning, but I will say, there are a lot of owners who are still being very cheap and not giving us professional athletes what we need."

She also described what characteristics the new commissioner should have.

"You need to have great character that is willing to withstand it all and uphold your values and what's best for the players," Cunningham said (29:30 mark). "It's definitely someone who is in great communication with the players, because at the end of the day, we should be joining forces; we should be growing this league to the best of our abilities."

Cunningham's Fever has had a tremendous season that has them looking like contenders as the postseason nears. Clark is the lifeblood of the offense, and Cunningham said her game has evolved in her third season in the league, specifically when it comes to getting in the paint.

"I really do feel like this year she is using her body so so well," Cunningham said (39:30 mark). "And she's using the glass, her jump shots are going in, and it's efficient, and it's good for us. But I do think that her body control this year has been huge."

The Fever are currently sitting in fifth place in the WNBA standings at 26-14 and have secured a playoff spot. They'll begin what they hope to be a deep postseason run in the coming weeks.

articles.title: Spain basketball star Megan DiLeo weighs in on Caitlin Clark's World Cup bench role ahead of semifinal
articles.summary: Megan DiLeo helped recruit Caitlin Clark to Iowa, but now the Spain center aims to upset her former school's star in the FIBA World Cup semifinal.
articles.body: BERLIN — Megan DiLeo will be looking to lead Team Spain to an upset win over the U.S. in the FIBA Women's World Cup semifinal on Saturday. That means she will be taking on her old friend Caitlin Clark. But DiLeo, Spain's star center and a 2025 WNBA champion with the Las Vegas Aces, may have to wait for Clark to come off the bench before seeing her on the hardwood. USA coach Kara Lawson has opted to start veteran Chelsea Gray over Clark at point guard for the U.S.'s first four games, despite Clark putting up superior numbers and playing more minutes. But DiLeo doesn't believe that Clark not starting will make things any easier for Spain on Saturday. TEAM USA COACH REVEALS IF CAITLIN CLARK WILL START IN THE WORLD CUP FINAL STAGE AFTER BENCH ROLE IN GROUP PLAY When asked if Clark not starting on Saturday will put Team Spain at an advantage, DiLeo said, "No, I don't think so. She's just a great player, it doesn't really matter when she goes into a game, she's going to make an impact." DiLeo added, "We just gotta be ready for her and for the rest of the roster. They're talented, they're deep. It kind of doesn't really matter who comes in." Saturday will be a reunion for the two Iowa alumni, as DiLeo played for the Hawkeyes from 2015-19, before Clark showed up on campus one year later. DiLeo said Friday that she helped recruit Clark to Iowa back then. "I was actually part of the recruiting process that she was kind of going through, figuring out where she wanted to go, as far as that, and she chose Iowa," DiLeo said. "Whenever I go back to visit campus and stuff and she was still playing we would get to interact and stuff, we check in on eachother every once in a while now. Just super happy we get to represent Iowa." DiLeo added that she hasn't spoken to Clark since they arrived in Germany for the World Cup due to scheduling constraints, but she's "excited" to see Clark on Saturday. DiLeo won consensus National Player of the Year honors in 2019 and finished her college career with 2,804 points and a school-record 1,460 rebounds. Iowa later retired her No. 10. Clark became a two-time consensus National Player of the Year and finished her career with 3,951 points, the most in NCAA Division I basketball history. Saturday will not be the first time they have faced each other internationally. The U.S. defeated Spain 84-70 during the World Cup qualifying tournament in Puerto Rico in March. DiLeo scored 15 points for Spain, while Clark finished with seven points and seven assists. Clark was later named the tournament’s most valuable player after leading the Americans to a 5-0 record. DiLeo became a naturalized Spanish citizen in 2023 and made her debut for Spain at the 2024 Paris Olympics. She averaged 18 points and 9.3 rebounds during that tournament and has remained one of the country’s most important interior players. Spain will enter as a significant underdog based on the countries’ history. The U.S. has won all 11 previous meetings listed by FIBA, including the 2014 World Cup championship game and the gold-medal game at the 2016 Rio Olympics. The Americans have also won 34 consecutive World Cup games since losing to Russia in the 2006 semifinals. They are two victories away from claiming a fifth straight World Cup championship.
