articles.title: U.S. Department of Justice reportedly opens criminal probe into dealings between Clippers, Kawhi Leonard
articles.summary: The same Brooklyn-based office that brought the case against Tim Donaghy and oversees the gambling probe involving Chauncey Billups is reportedly overseeing...
articles.body:
Dealings between the Los Angeles Clippers , Kawhi Leonard and third-party vendors are now under federal criminal investigation.

The New York Times reported Thursday that the U.S. Department of Justice has initiated its own investigation into the matter after an NBA probe determined that the Clippers, team owner Steve Ballmer and Leonard circumvented the league's salary cap via third-party deals that funneled tens of millions of dollars to the seven-time NBA All-Star.

Per the Times, the federal probe is being led by the U.S. attorney's Eastern District of New York office in Brooklyn , the same office that's previously investigated several high-profile sports-related criminal matters.

That same office worked with the FBI in the 2007 case against disgraced former NBA referee Tim Donaghy, who admitted to betting on games that he'd officiated. It's also brought charges against multiple professional athletes in a wide-reaching probe into alleged illegal gambling, including former NBA All-Star Chauncey Billups and All-Star Cleveland Guardians closer Emmanuel Clase .

Per the Times, the "inquiry's scope, targets and the possible crimes being examined were unclear." Prosecutors have issued at least one subpoena, according to the report. Sources told the Times that it's unclear if the probe will result in criminal charges.

NBA probe resulted in punitive discipline for Clippers, Steve Ballmer

News of the federal probe breaks eight days after the NBA released the findings of its investigation that was conducted by independent law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz . Per the NBA, "the investigation found a pattern of misconduct and multiple significant rules violations by the Clippers organization, a prior offender of the salary cap circumvention rules."

The NBA responded with some of the most punitive discipline in league history. It stripped the Clippers of five first-round draft picks in consecutive years from 2029-33, a crippling measure for the franchise's competitive prospects.

The NBA fined Ballmer $30 million and suspended him "from all league and team activities for one year" in addition to handing out suspensions to multiple Clippers executives. The league also fined Leonard $700,000 and banned his uncle and business partner Dennis Robertson from engaging in NBA business dealings for five years.

Via multiple statements, the Clippers and, by proxy, Ballmer have vowed to fight the NBA's findings and to explore "every legal remedy to address this gross injustice."

"We vehemently reject the NBA's findings, which are the result of a heavily biased investigation seeking to justify a predetermined narrative rather than facts and evidence," the Clippers wrote in response to the league's findings that were announced on Sept. 2. "What the league told us privately differs from what it announced today publicly, and they have not held themselves close to the standard Commissioner [Adam] Silver set at the start of this investigation to ensure its fairness and accuracy."

Leonard wrote the following in response to the league's findings:

"Integrity and respect for this game are fundamental to who I am," Leonard wrote on social media. "I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family.

A spokesman for the U.S. attorney's office declined comment when asked by the Times about the federal probe, and the the Clippers and the NBA did not respond when asked for comment and confirmation that they'd received a subpoena, according to the report.

articles.title: Clippers face federal criminal probe after NBA punishes team over Kawhi Leonard deals
articles.summary: Federal prosecutors and a grand jury are now probing whether Steve Ballmer and the Los Angeles Clippers arranged secret deals to pay Kawhi Leonard.
articles.body: Federal prosecutors have launched a criminal investigation into allegations that the Los Angeles Clippers arranged secret, off-the-books sponsorship deals for Kawhi Leonard to circumvent the NBA’s salary cap, first reported by The New York Times. The inquiry is being handled by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of New York in Brooklyn, which has previously pursued major sports integrity cases involving NBA referee gambling and FIFA corruption. Federal authorities began scrutinizing the Clippers’ alleged conduct before the NBA announced its penalties, including a $30 million fine, the forfeiture of five consecutive first-round picks from 2029 through 2033 and a one-year suspension for owner Steve Ballmer. Two top Clippers executives also received suspensions. MALIK BEASLEY INDICTED ON FEDERAL CHARGES FOR ALLEGEDLY FIXING HIS OWN NBA PERFORMANCES FOR BETTORS The Times reported that a grand jury has already issued at least one subpoena in the investigation. Investigators are zeroing in on undisclosed endorsement deals, including a reported $28 million agreement with Aspiration Partners. The green finance company later collapsed into bankruptcy, while co-founder Joe Sanberg was sentenced to 14 years in federal prison for fraud. Prosecutors are examining whether Clippers owner Steve Ballmer and team executives helped facilitate side deals that compensated Leonard beyond the NBA’s salary-cap limits. The SEC has also entered the investigation. Daktronics, which supplied displays for the Clippers’ Intuit Dome, confirmed that regulators requested records tied to its sponsorship agreements with Leonard. The federal investigation significantly escalates the Clippers’ scandal, which the NBA called a "pattern of misconduct" after a yearlong review by the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. Leonard’s uncle and manager, Dennis Robertson, received a five-year ban from the NBA, while Leonard was ordered to pay $700,000 in restitution. The Clippers strongly rejected the NBA’s findings, accusing the league of conducting a biased investigation designed to justify a predetermined narrative. "We vehemently reject the NBA’s findings, which are the result of a heavily biased investigation seeking to justify a predetermined narrative rather than facts and evidence," the franchise said in a statement. The team added, "We intend to vigorously challenge these findings and penalties through every avenue available to us and look forward to an ethical and impartial arbitration process." David Kelley, Ballmer’s attorney, called the NBA’s investigation a "witch hunt" and a "gross injustice" in a letter to Commissioner Adam Silver. DODGERS OWNER MARK WALTER DENIES REPORTS, SAYS TEAM PAYROLL IS SUPPORTED BY REVENUE: 'THERE HAS BEEN NO FRAUD' Kelley argued that league officials privately acknowledged facts that contradicted the NBA’s public position. "League counsel has acknowledged in our discussions that the league does not believe there was an agreement between the Clippers and Aspiration to funnel money to Kawhi Leonard," Kelley wrote. He also emphasized that federal authorities previously determined Ballmer was "a victim of Joe Sanberg’s fraud, not a participant." Leonard defended his conduct while acknowledging mistakes by members of his inner circle. "Integrity and respect for this game are fundamental to who I am," Leonard said. "I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family." Leonard added that he entered into his Clippers contract and the other agreements "in good faith," with no knowledge of any effort to circumvent the salary cap. Ballmer and the Clippers are considering a federal lawsuit against the NBA to block the sanctions. The criminal investigation could complicate that effort. Civil litigation may be delayed if key witnesses invoke their Fifth Amendment rights against self-incrimination. Spokespersons for the U.S. Attorney’s Office, the Clippers and the NBA declined to comment on the investigation. articles.title: Newly minted $12.4 million Timberwolves star reveals why he chose Anthony Edwards’ team over Lakers: “I wanted to go to a winning culture”
articles.summary: NBA News: Jonathan Kuminga has finally made his choice after entering NBA free agency with several teams interested in his services. The newly minted Minnesota .
articles.body: Jonathan Kuminga has finally made his choice after entering NBA free agency with several teams interested in his services. The newly minted Minnesota Timberwolves star chose Anthony Edwards’ team over the Los Angeles Lakers, even though reports indicated Los Angeles was prepared to offer him more money. For Kuminga, the appeal was less about the biggest contract and more about finding the right place to win. His decision also gives him a chance to join a young Minnesota group with high expectations for the upcoming season.Kuminga explained his thinking during his introductory press conference in Minnesota, pointing to the Timberwolves’ recent success and the atmosphere around the franchise. The 23-year-old also spoke about his desire to help the team win while keeping his attention on the present rather than making predictions about his long-term future.Minnesota Timberwolves land Jonathan KumingaThe Timberwolves agreed to a two-year, $12.4 million deal with Kuminga this offseason, according to ESPN. The contract includes a $6.3 million player option for the second season, giving him an important decision after the upcoming campaign.Kuminga could enter free agency again next offseason or choose to return for the 2026-27 NBA season. Much will depend on how his first year in Minnesota goes and how well he fits alongside Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels and Rudy Gobert.The move gives Minnesota an NBA champion who already has significant experience despite being only 23. His agent, Aaron Turner, said Kuminga had a clear preference after considering his options.Jonathan Kuminga reveals why he picked Timberwolves over the LakersKuminga had several suitors during free agency, with the Lakers among the teams reportedly competing most seriously for him. Chicago and Portland were also listed among his other options.The decision to choose Minnesota became more notable because Kuminga reportedly turned down more lucrative opportunities. A one-year structure within the deal also gives him a path back to free agency, but Kuminga focused on something else when asked about his choice."I think this was the best decision for me," he said. "I just wanted to go to a winning culture. I think this was one of the best winning cultures I could have chose out of all the options. I spoke to so many people on this team, including front office, coaches, some of the players, and the vibe was just the type of vibe I was looking for."Minnesota has built a strong recent record under Tim Connelly and Chris Finch. The Timberwolves have made five straight playoff appearances and won at least one series in three consecutive seasons, including two trips to the Western Conference finals.Over the past three seasons, Minnesota has gone 154-92 with 24 playoff wins. The Lakers have gone 150-96 during the same span but have six playoff victories. Kuminga's decision, therefore, reflects the current direction of the two teams rather than their historic resumes."I would say it's one of the best decisions I've made, just looking at the roster, looking at the young group of guys they have," Kuminga said. "Seeing what they've done in the past and things they're trying to accomplish going forward. I think I fit well with this culture and I can come here and help win as many games as we can."I think the choice was, we're trying to win. Trying to help winning. That's why I made this decision."Jonathan Kuminga showers praise for new teammate LaMelo BallKuminga also offered an early glimpse at what excites him about his new teammates, particularly Ball. The Timberwolves added the star guard via a trade with the Charlotte Hornets, and Kuminga said he was impressed by Ball's passing during a workout.“I was watching him work out yesterday. I was watching him doing certain things, and just the way he passed the ball, it’s incredible,” Kuminga said of Ball. “I mean, I’ve played with so many point guards in my career, but I never played with somebody that could pass as good as LaMelo. So, I think I’m looking forward to it, and I’m excited.”Kuminga previously played with elite point guards Chris Paul and Stephen Curry, making his praise for Ball notable. His comment also adds another layer to the expectations surrounding Minnesota after an active offseason.For now, Kuminga is focused on making the most of his opportunity. articles.title: Megan Rapinoe says women's sports are facing 'regression' of 'equal rights' in new Kamala Harris interview
articles.summary: Kamala Harris joined Megan Rapinoe for a new interview touching on women's sports, politics, and a puzzling tangent about "the boy next door."
articles.body: You thought Kamala Harris was done after getting summarily beaten in the 2024 presidential election by Donald Trump? Think again. The former vice president is right back at it, laughing it up with friends, discussing her future in politics, and avoiding any and all difficult questions she does not have prepared answers to. On Thursday, Harris joined former US women’s soccer player and political activist Megan Rapinoe for a fawning new interview on "Why Are You Like This?" where she touched on important questions, like, "Why are you so amazing?" SMUG MEGAN RAPINOE GOES ON UNHINGED RANT, ATTACKS RILEY GAINES AND SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM OVER WOMEN'S SPORTS "You could do anything, you’re brilliant, and you’re talented, and you’re beautiful, and you’re smart, and you’re funny and you’re all these things," Rapinoe said in an incredible moment of journalism. The context for this question is Rapinoe's wondering why Harris chose to go into politics because she would be reminded that she’s "still a woman" and "still black." Her answer? Well, not much. Determination, enjoying hard work, and some barrier breaking, of course. As for her upbringing, Harris said that she was taken to "marches" in a "stroller" by her parents, which she associates with her educational and political choices later on. While the interview is light on important topics around women’s sports, Rapinoe couldn’t help herself when talking about her own experiences and what we’ve supposedly lost since her playing career ended. "I’m thinking about my own experience being a female athlete, and I went through, in the prime of my career, just the most historic time in women’s sports," she said. "I mean, it was crazy in the best ways. We saw a huge amount of progress, which has led into a pretty significant regression in terms of just equal rights and people’s rights in general. I definitely think those two are tied." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE What rights have women in sports lost? Is she implying that because there are now limitations on males in women's sports, women are losing their rights? The reality is precisely the reverse. Had a male athlete occupied Rapinoe's spot on the US women's soccer team, she would never have achieved the level of success and the accomplishments that defined her career. Not to mention that male athletes are not prevented from playing sports, they're simply required to play sports against other males. That's the only reasonable and rational position, which is why Rapinoe opposes it so fiercely. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Rapinoe then tries to tie women's sports being "different" to men's sports to governing "as a woman," to which Harris laughs aggressively, then responds with, "Well, I've always been a woman, so I don't know what to tell you," which about sums up the level of scintillating intellectual discussion present throughout the episode. Harris then goes on a fascinatingly inept tangent, saying that in order to describe her experience as a woman in politics, she wants Rapinoe to close her eyes and picture someone based on four words: "the boy next door." "Now you have a sense of what he looks like," Harris continues. He probably plays softball, he probably lives somewhere in suburban America. He's a good kid." STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW! Do boys play softball? What is she talking about? Harris brings the comparison home by saying, "What four words together in our language would describe you or me?," then adds, "we don't have it." Well, there are plenty of four-word phrases to describe Megan Rapinoe and Kamala Harris actually, just none that they would like. Later in the interview, Harris says that "We have increasingly witnessed a concentration of wealth and power among a few, to the exclusion of the most, and that wealth and concentration being also a political power." Obviously, Harris is excluded from this, despite being an extremely wealthy woman who just purchased an $8 million house in Malibu with a heated pool and in-ground spa. Joe Biden is excluded from this, despite his decades-long career in politics and his son, Hunter, using his influence with the former vice president and eventual president to increase his wealth. Barack Obama is excluded from this, despite owning multiple mansions, including a beautiful Martha's Vineyard estate. As for whether the very wealthy Harris will run again for the 2028 nomination? She hasn't decided, she told Rapinoe. God help us all if she does. The interview as a whole illustrates a central reason Harris fell short in 2024: her campaign and her party were, and continue to be, represented by figures such as Rapinoe. Who believe that males should play in women's sports and that every day is an opportunity for grievance. Harris has no meaningful insights to make about herself, politics, or how to improve the country. Only vague hand waving about the need to change things. Whatever that might mean. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD There's been no "regression" in women's rights in recent years, and if anything, the rise in popularity for sports like the WNBA has made it more obvious how important it is to protect those athletes. Both physically and in terms of competitive fairness. Rapinoe can't accept that, because it undermines her and Harris' worldview. Reality often does.

articles.title: Lakers champion and Hall of Famer Dwight Howard makes surprising return to basketball in a bold career move after NAB retirement
articles.summary: NBA News: Dwight Howard is coming out of retirement, and he's doing it more than 6,000 miles from home. The 40-year-old Hall of Famer has signed with Black Fort.
articles.body: Dwight Howard is coming out of retirement, and he's doing it more than 6,000 miles from home. The 40-year-old Hall of Famer has signed with Black Fortress Tbilisi, a club in the country of Georgia, and will join the team when its season opens in October.The signing comes barely six months after Howard announced he was walking away from the sport for good, and less than a week after he turned up in an exhibition game in Mongolia. Contract terms haven't been made public, but the move gives newly promoted Black Fortress an internationally known face for its top-flight debut.Dwight Howard returns to basketball and will play in GeorgiaBlack Fortress confirmed the deal this week, sharing a photo of Dwight Howard in the club's black and orange No. 12 jersey along with the caption "It's official. Signed." The Georgian Super League side earned its spot in the top division after winning the second-tier title, and landing a name like Howard's gives it instant visibility heading into its first season among the country's elite clubs.Howard broke the news himself a little earlier, leaning into the coincidence that he was born in the U.S. state of Georgia and is now headed to the country that shares its name. "Georgia, here I come," he wrote, adding that fans should keep an eye out for what Black Fortress brings to the court once October arrives.Financial details of the contract, including its length, haven't been disclosed by either party.Howard's long, unlikely road since leaving the NBAHoward last played in the league during the 2021-22 season with the Los Angeles Lakers. Since then his career has taken him through Taiwan, where he put up big numbers for the Taoyuan Leopards, and to Dubai, where he helped a Philippines-based squad reach the final of an international tournament. He also spent a season in the BIG3 with the Los Angeles Riot.In March, Howard said he was stepping away from the game entirely to spend more time with his family. That decision didn't last through the summer. Earlier this month he posted that he was headed to Asia, then shared photos from Mongolia, where he suited up for the SG Apes in a preseason game just days before the Black Fortress deal was announced.The 40-year-old was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2025, capping a career that included eight All-Star selections and five All-NBA nods. He also won three Defensive Player of the Year awards and a championship ring with the Lakers in 2020, his third stint with the franchise.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “Can they get any more disrespectful?”: LA Clippers wrapped in another ugly controversy after Chris Paul decision who played 21 years in NBA
articles.summary: NBA News: The Los Angeles Clippers have picked a fresh fight with their own history. Chris Paul's old No. 3, the number he wore for six seasons that turned the .
articles.body: The Los Angeles Clippers have picked a fresh fight with their own history. Chris Paul's old No. 3, the number he wore for six seasons that turned the franchise into a real playoff team, is heading to Bradley Beal for the coming season. The decision lands on an organization already reeling from the league's punishment in the Kawhi Leonard cap circumvention case, and it has reopened a wound from Paul's messy exit last season. Beal has responded publicly, but the backlash from fans hasn't slowed down.Clippers make bold roster call despite promise made to Chris PaulNBA reporter Etienne Catalan first flagged the move this week. With Beal returning to the Clippers for the 2026-27 season, the team plans to give him Paul's old No. 3, a number the Clippers' own team store has already listed for Beal heading into the year.That contradicts what Paul says he was told. Appearing on Carmelo Anthony's "7 PM in Brooklyn" podcast, Paul said the organization had promised to retire the number once he stepped away from the game. The Clippers have never retired a single jersey in their history, and Paul, who called his exit "most disrespectful," says the number now sitting on Beal's back is proof the team never meant to keep its word.The backdrop makes it worse. Paul spent six seasons building the Clippers into a perennial playoff team during his first stint, then returned for a second run in 2025 that ended badly. He was reportedly informed in the middle of the night that the team was moving on from him, then sent home in December amid claims he was undermining the coaching staff, a characterization he disputed.Bradley Beal responds to Clippers controversy over Chris PaulWhen Paul signed with the Clippers in 2025, Beal voluntarily gave up the No. 3 he had worn his entire career so Paul could keep the number tied to his "CP3" identity. Team president Lawrence Frank called it "such a great gesture" at the time, saying Beal wanted to hand over the number before Paul even knew about it.With that goodwill now looking undone, Beal took to social media to get ahead of the criticism. He called Paul "a legend," and added that his history and brand with the franchise could never be erased. The message reads less like a man trying to justify wearing the number and more like someone caught in the middle of a situation he didn't create.NBA fans react to Clippers controversyFans weren't as forgiving. Reaction poured in across social media once the news about the 21-year NBA legend spread.@CKenzyNelson wrote: "We can't be mad at Bradley Beal for wearing No. 3 with the Los Angeles Clippers. The Clippers allowed him to wear it 🤷🏽‍♂️ For some reason, they seem to hate Chris Paul, even after everything he did for that franchise 🤦🏽‍♂️🏀"@cmonnowplayaman asked simply: "Why take the number then lmao"@CanyonDriver joked: "Revenge plot for CP3 if he's a GM for the Lakers. smoovay"@Slime5ea5on summed up the mood: "Can they get any more disrespectful lol"@crmnchin6969 didn't hold back: "clippers cant do anything right. will always be the lakers little bro"And @curgoat09 wasn't buying Beal's message either: "'He's a legend' still got that number on though"The Clippers can’t catch a break. articles.title: Gym change? No problem. Harrisburg tops Dell Rapids
articles.summary: DELL RAPIDS, S.D. (KELO) — In one of the strangest volleyball games ever, Class AA number one Harrisburg topped Class A number two Dell Rapids, 3-1, after th...
articles.body:
DELL RAPIDS, S.D. (KELO) — In one of the strangest volleyball games ever, Class AA number one Harrisburg topped Class A number two Dell Rapids, 3-1, after the teams and fans changed gyms in the middle of the second set due to a falling basketball hoop.

A cable holding one of the hoops to the ceiling snapped off as Harrisburg was about to serve.

The hoop came down into position with a loud crash, but thankfully stayed attached to the ceiling and did not cause any injuries.

After a brief delay in which referees and coaches from both teams discussed what to do next, it was decided the game would be moved to the middle school at a greatly reduced fan capacity.

Harrisburg went on to win the stop/start second set to take a 2-0 lead.

Dell Rapids won set three to avoid the sweep but fell in set four to lose to match.

Up next, Harrisburg has eight days off before heading to the Durango Classic in Las Vegas September 18-19 while Dell Rapids hosts Canton on Tuesday.

articles.title: DOJ Reportedly Probing LA Clippers Salary Cap Scandal After NBA Suspends Steve Ballmer
articles.summary: It's unclear if the probe will lead to criminal charges but the report comes just a week after the NBA handed down a series of harsh punishments against the...
articles.body:
The Justice Department has initiated a criminal investigation into allegations that the Los Angeles Clippers used secret endorsement deals to boost its star player Kawhi Leonard 's income while violating the NBA's salary cap, the New York Times reported , just a week after the league suspended the team's billionaire owner Steve Ballmer for a year.

Citing unnamed sources briefed on the matter, the Times reported that the matter is being investigated by prosecutors in the U.S. Attorney's Office in Brooklyn and the probe is in its "earliest stages."

The report noted that prosecutors have already issued a subpoena as part of the probe, but details of the crimes being investigated remain unclear.

The DOJ investigation began before the NBA handed out its own punishments against the Clippers—including a year-long suspension of the team's owner and ninth-richest person in the world.

The Clippers and the NBA have not yet publicly commented on the reported probe.

What Do We Know About The SEC Probe Into The Clippers Scandal?

The Securities and Exchange Commission has also sought information from Daktronics, the electronic signage and scoreboard company, about its alleged endorsement deal with Leonard, the company disclosed last week. Daktronics Chief Financial Officer Howard Atkins said in the company's earnings call: "We have received requests for information from the NBA. Additionally, the Securities and Exchange Commission is seeking information from us concerning the company and Mr. Leonard." Atkins said the company takes the requests seriously and is cooperating, but won't comment further. The third-party probe commissioned by the NBA found that Daktronics and two other firms had paid Leonard $18 million by August 2021 as part of "highly unusual" endorsement agreements.

Last week, the NBA announced a series of punishments against the Clippers and Ballmer after ordering a third-party probe on the matter. The historic ban handed to Ballmer was for him trying to help Leonard "obtain off-court income opportunities" and for "approving a business deal that he knew was a precondition" for fintech company Aspiration to agree to an endorsement deal with Leonard. The Clippers were also hit with a $30 million fine and stripped of five first-round draft picks from the 2029, 2030, 2031, 2032 and 2033 NBA Drafts. Leonard avoided suspension but was ordered to pay the league $700,000 in restitution. The star forward is expected to join the Toronto Raptors for the upcoming season.

articles.title: Stephon Castle showcases his gratitude for the Spurs legends' impactful support
articles.summary: Stephon Castle loves how the former Spurs players help the current ones.
articles.body:
Across the NBA, there are plenty of iconic franchises. One of them is the San Antonio Spurs , a team with a history of success. They have won five championships in their time in the NBA, and their legends continue to stick around and help the next generation.

People like Tim Duncan , Manu Ginobili , David Robinson, and many more are always present for the Spurs . This has helped the younger players because they know that they have some mentors to go to when they need help.

Stephon Castle is thankful for former Spurs players' support

For any Spurs player, they will become familiar with the older figures within the organization who have been there for a long time. Of course, Gregg Popovich is probably the most recognizable one, as he is still the team president.

Mitch Johnson might have taken over as the head coach, but Pop still has an impact and influence on the players. Youngsters like Castle and Dylan Harper are benefiting from this because they know they have mentors to look up to.

Castle himself has only been in the league for two seasons, but he has learned plenty of lessons already. Not only on the court, but from those who have succeeded already, like Duncan and Ginobili.

"It's a blessing to play for an organization like that. The greats that we've had come through that organization. I mean, what they still do for that organization to this day. They come back, they give us tips. You know, they watch our games. They're at our practices all the time," Castle said on Slam Philippines .

It is a big deal for the Spurs to have this kind of culture because it will only get better with time. Since they are focused on building towards the future with this current core, the older core are putting in a concerted effort to help the team succeed moving forward.

articles.body: Lorenzo Brown, jugador de origen estadounidense internacional con España, ha roto su silencio sobre su situación con el Olimpia Milano. Lorenzo Brown se nacionalizó por carta de naturaleza aprobada por el Consejo de Ministros en 2022 y debutó con España en el Eurobasket 2022 colgándose la medalla de oro. El bautizado como 'Lorenzo de Albacete', que brilló con 29 puntos ante Alemania en semifinales y fue fundamental con sus asistencias para ayudar a Willy Hernangómez para ser el MVP del torneo, fue elegido miembro del 'Quinteto Ideal' del EuroBasket. Que son bases sobre las que nunca se puede basar un debate. ¿Ha habido xenofobia con Lorenzo Brown? Desde luego". Lorenzo Brown fue importante para España en el Torneo Preolímpico y defendió a 'La Familia' en los Juegos Olímpicos de París 2024. El de Rockford (Illinois) no pudo disputar el Eurobasket de 2025 con España por culpa de unos problemas familiares.

articles.standfirst: El pívot, de 40 años, anuncia en redes sociales su llegada a los Black Fortress Tbilisi, que acaban de ascender a la Superliga georgiana
articles.summary: El pívot anuncia en redes sociales su llegada a los Black Fortress Tbilisi, que acaban de ascender a la Superliga georgiana
articles.body: Dwight Howard va a jugar en Georgia. Pero no en la Georgia en la que nació hace 40 años, pues es natural de Atlanta. En la Georgia país. El pívot, que recientemente había anunciado su retirada, volverá a las canchas para enrolarse en los Black Fortress Tbilisi, conjunto que acaba de ascender a la Superliga del país caucásico. En las redes sociales, el propio jugador bromeaba con su destino y su origen: "¡Georgia, voy para allá! No a mi casa en Atlanta, Georgia, sino a Tiblisi, Georgia". La última vez que Howard jugó al baloncesto profesional fue para los Taoyuan Taiwan Beer Leopards en Taiwán en la temporada 22-23. También había tenido pasos por Dubái y Mongolia. Ahora sumará un nuevo destino exótico en el que está por ver el grado de compromiso que adquiere con su nuevo club, al que ha puesto en el mapa mundial. "He decidido, al ver un lugar en el que realmente quieren que esté allí, que traslade mi energía. Así que es oficial: 'Superman' está de camino hacia Georgia”, continuaba el pívot. Se suponía que Howard había colgado la capa de superhéroe en marzo de este año después de ser uno de los pívots más dominantes de la NBA en el siglo XXI. Elegido por los Magic en el primer puesto del draft de 2004, puso a la franquicia de Orlando en lo alto de la Conferencia Este y después de ocho años se marcharía a los Lakers, con los que no fue todo aquello que parecía. Tras salir de Los Ángeles jugó en los Rockets, los Hawks, los Hornets, los Wizards y volvió a los Lakers para ganar el anillo en 2020, la temporada del COVID, cuando el título se decidió en la burbuja que se creó en Disney World. Recalaría más tarde en los Sixers y aún tendría una efímera tercera etapa con el conjunto angelino en la campaña 21-22. Su último partido en la NBA data del 8 de abril de 2022. Entre los méritos que se encuentra en la carrera de Howard están tres galardones de mejor defensor de la NBA, sus cinco inclusiones en el mejor quinteto defensivo, sus cinco temporadas como mejor reboteador, otras tres en la que fue el mejor taponador y sus ocho presencias en el All Star. Su imagen más icónica fue su participación en el concurso de mates con una capa de Supermán. Ganó la edición de 2008. Internacional con Estados Unidos, formó parte de la selección que fue bronce en el Mundial de Saitama en 2006 ganado por España y del equipo formado para recuperar el trono planetario en los Juegos de Pekín en 2008. Como reconocimiento a su carrera, el pívot fue incluido en el Hall of Fame el año pasado.

articles.title: Una semifinal del Mundial con el corazón dividido: Marta Xargay, entre su selección y su pareja
articles.standfirst: La exinternacional, ganadora de siete medallas con España, está casada con Breanna Stewart, estrella de la selección de Estados Unidos
articles.summary: La exinternacional, ganadora de siete medallas con España, está casada con Breanna Stewart, estrella de la selección de Estados Unidos
articles.body: La semifinal del Mundial Femenino de este sábado entre España y Estados Unidos (20.00 horas) será muy especial para Marta Xargay. La exjugadora tendrá el corazón dividido. Por un lado estará la selección española con la que tantos éxitos conquistó. Por otro, la selección estadounidense con Breanna Stewart, su pareja, como gran estrella. Durante el Mundial, la exinternacional española lanzaba mensajes de ánimo a la que fuera su selección. "Confiad en vuestro trabajo, que lo estáis 'petando'. Seguid juntas, como equipo, como una piña", decía a los medios oficiales de la FEB en una charla en la que recordaba sus éxitos: "Ha sido parte de mi vida y vuelven esos recuerdos tan bonitos. Estoy contenta por lo vivido y por lo que estamos viviendo". Este sábado, sin embargo, tendrá muchos sentimientos encontrados. Xargay, de 35 años, fue integrante de la mejor generación del baloncesto femenino español. Con la selección se colgó siete medallas: tres oros Europeos, la plata de los Juegos de Río, la plata del Mundial de 2014, el bronce del Mundial de 2018, ganado por la que acabaría siendo su pareja, y otro bronce continental. Stewart, mientras, está considerada como una de las mejores jugadoras de la historia. Su abrumador palmarés incluye tres títulos de la WNBA y cuatro campeonatos de la NCAA. Con la selección estadounidense suma ya tres oros olímpicos y otros tantos mundiales. También tiene relación con el seleccionador español Miguel Méndez, a cuyas órdenes ganó dos de sus tres Euroligas: 2021 con el Ekaterinburg y esta temporada con el Fenerbahce. Y con Raquel Carrera, compañera en las New York Liberty. En el presente Mundial, la ala-pívot de 32 años y 1,91 metros está promediando 9,8 puntos, 7,0 rebotes y 2,8 asistencias para ser, con 15,8 créditos, la jugadora más valorada de un combinado estadounidense que lleva ya 73 victorias seguidas en torneos planetarios desde 2006. Las dos jugadoras coincidieron en el Dynamo Kursk durante la temporada 2018-19. Ahí comenzó su relación. Se comprometieron en mayo de 2021 y se casaron en julio de ese mismo año. Pocos días después, Xargay anunciaba que dejaba definitivamente el baloncesto tras haber parado temporalmente un año antes. La pareja tiene dos hijos, Ruby y Theo, que no se pierden ninguno de los éxitos de Stewart y que estos días están también en Berlín.

articles.summary: Los vitorianos trabajan en la contratación del pívot ucraniano que llegó al conjunto blanco a mitad de la temporada pasada
articles.body: El Kosner Baskonia trabaja para reforzar su corto juego interior y el principal candidato a incorporarse al equipo es Alex Len. El pívot ucraniano de 33 años y 2,13 metros se encuentra actualmente sin equipo después de haber salido del Real Madrid, donde llegó a mitad de la temporada pasada. Su fichaje por el conjunto vitoriano, según ha informado 'El Correo', está cerca. El club baskonista está necesitado de al menos dos refuerzos en la pintura tras la marcha de Khalifa Diop a los Cavaliers. Para el puesto de '5', sólo dispone de Kenneth Faried, recientemente llegado a Vitoria y ya ejercitándose con el equipo. Tadas Sedekerskis, Rodions Kurucs y Clement Frisch podrían ejercer como parches interiores. La posible llegada de Len aliviaría en partes esos problemas. El jugador ucraniano llegó al Real Madrid en octubre del año pasado como recambio de Bruno Fernando. Disputó 46 encuentros con el conjunto madridista con medias de 7,1 y 3,6 rebotes en la Liga Endesa mientras que en la Euroliga bajó sus estadísticas a 3,0 y 2,0, respectivamente. No pudo ser importante a la sombra de Edy Tavares y cuando tuvo oportunidad tras la lesión de rodilla del caboverdiano, él también sufrió problemas físicos en la fascia plantar del pie izquierdo. El interior ucraniano tiene experiencia en la NBA pues antes de firmar por el Madrid pasó 12 temporadas en la Liga profesional estadounidense. En ese tiempo disputó 690 encuentros entre Suns, Hawks, Kings, Raptors, Wizards y Lakers. Sus promedios allí fueron de 6,7 puntos y 5,3 rebotes por partido.

articles.title: “You try to keep things as sacred as you can”: How LeBron James and Savannah James quietly protected daughter Zhuri James’ childhood from the spotlight before introducing her to the world
articles.summary: NBA News: LeBron James and Savannah James have spent much of their lives in front of cameras, but they never felt their children had to share every part of that.
articles.body: LeBron James and Savannah James have spent much of their lives in front of cameras, but they never felt their children had to share every part of that experience. When their daughter Zhuri James was born on October 22, 2014, the couple kept her early childhood largely private. It was a deliberate choice for their youngest child, who entered a family already surrounded by enormous attention because of LeBron’s NBA career and her older brothers, Bronny James and Bryce James. Why LeBron James and Savannah James kept Zhuri James away from public attentionSavannah James explained the family’s decision during Vanity Fair’s September 13, 2022 profile of the James family. Looking back at the years when Zhuri was a baby, Savannah said, “You try to keep things as sacred as you can.” She then gave a rare explanation of just how carefully she and LeBron handled their daughter’s early exposure, saying, “Back when she was born, we didn’t show her. No one saw her until LeBron won his 2016 championship”Savannah was not saying that Zhuri’s birth had been kept secret. Her arrival was publicly reported in October 2014. What she meant was that the family chose not to put their baby daughter on display during those first years. That distinction is important because LeBron’s life already attracted intense attention, and even ordinary family moments could quickly become public.The couple had two sons growing up alongside Zhuri, too. Bronny James and Bryce James were already connected to basketball because of their father, while LeBron remained one of the most recognizable athletes in the world. Zhuri, however, received a quieter introduction to that life. Savannah later summed up the family’s approach during the same conversation by saying, “Everything isn’t for everybody.” It was a simple way of explaining why the James family did not feel obligated to show the public every part of their home life. LeBron James’ 2016 championship brought Zhuri James into the spotlightOn June 19, 2016, LeBron James and the Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Golden State Warriors 93-89 in Game 7 of the NBA Finals. Cleveland completed a historic comeback from a 3-1 deficit and won the franchise’s first NBA championship. During the celebration that followed, Zhuri became part of a huge public moment alongside her father.Savannah later pointed to that championship as the occasion when people finally saw Zhuri publicly. She was only 20 months old, and her appearance came during one of the happiest nights of LeBron’s career rather than through a carefully planned celebrity introduction. That made the moment feel more like a family memory that happened to unfold in front of millions of viewers.As Zhuri grew older, the James family allowed her personality to come through naturally. By the time Vanity Fair profiled the family in September 2022, Zhuri had her own YouTube lifestyle show, All Things Zhuri, where she explored interests such as baking, yoga and painting. Savannah even called her the family’s “in-house creative director.Savannah also explained that none of her children had been pushed toward basketball simply because their father was LeBron James. During the same interview, she said, “With LeBron being their dad, it’s just automatic. It’s not something we’ve pushed or told them that they had to do, or anything like that. It just happened.” That approach gave Zhuri room to develop interests that were separate from her father’s career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham launches new podcast after previous co-host shared opposing views on trans athletes
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham launched her "No Hesitation" podcast with Drew Hanlen, offering blunt takes on WNBA media coverage, award voting and Caitlin Clark.
articles.body: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham has returned to podcasting with a new co-host after her previous partner publicly shared an opposing position to Cunningham on the topic of transgender athletes in women’s sports. Cunningham launched "No Hesitation" alongside prominent basketball trainer Drew Hanlen on Thursday. The program replaces "Show Me Something," the podcast she previously hosted with "Summer House" personality West Wilson. "Show Me Something" stopped releasing episodes this summer. Its social media accounts and YouTube channel have since been rebranded under the "No Hesitation" name. Neither Cunningham, Wilson nor The Volume has publicly said the disagreement over transgender athletes caused the change or formally explained Wilson’s departure. SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM AND WEST WILSON SPLIT ON TRANSGENDER ATHLETES IN GIRLS' SPORTS DESPITE PODCAST PARTNERSHIP Wilson publicly shared his opposing view on the trans athlete issue, shortly after an ESPN profile reported her belief that women’s sports should remain reserved for biological females. Wilson called transgender participation in American sports a "borderline non-existent issue" and accused conservatives, politicians, athletes and news organizations of portraying transgender people as a disproportionate threat. Cunningham, meanwhile, stood by her position. "I said what I said. I think it’s common sense," she told reporters in July. "I think I’ll always believe in that. It’s really important to protect children, and that’s little girls who are also involved in that category." Cunningham has repeatedly said she does not hate transgender people and believes there is room to love everyone. However, she has also maintained that the rights, safety and opportunities of biological women must be protected. Cunningham and Hanlen did not discuss Wilson or the transgender-athlete dispute during the debut episode of "No Hesitation." Instead, Cunningham introduced the new show as a place for candid basketball discussions. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "I just felt like there was not a podcast or really any social media out there that gave you real, honest truth about basketball and strictly basketball," Cunningham said. Hanlen acknowledged the political attention Cunningham has attracted and suggested the public often receives a distorted impression of her. "People think you’re like some troll and make statements, but really it’s 99% of the time people ask you a question, you answer, you give your opinion, and then people blow it up and act like you made a big political statement," Hanlen said. "Stop asking me questions if you don’t want the truth," Cunningham responded. The conversation later turned to the way the WNBA and its players are covered. Cunningham said media attention and award voting can be driven by popularity and politics instead of on-court performance. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "I think it’s very political," Cunningham said. "I think there’s a lot of people who are really, really great who don’t get the credit because maybe they don’t have the popularity or they don’t have the platform." "I don’t know if there’s voting fatigue," she added. "I just don’t know how accurate the voting is at times." Cunningham also agreed with Hanlen’s contention that WNBA media members frequently prioritize subjects other than basketball. "I think you kind of hit it when you said the WNBA media pretty much covers everything but basketball," Cunningham said. She later called on WNBA reporters to emphasize the league’s players and their achievements. "Now it’s on the WNBA media to actually tell the good stories, to tell the positive stories, to actually talk about basketball and how freaking awesome our league is playing this year," Cunningham said. "History is being made this year." Cunningham’s position echoed comments she made during the controversy over transgender participation. She said in August that she wanted to "get back to basketball" and argued the sport was being played at its highest level. ESPN reported at the time that rallies and counterprotests had followed the Fever on the road after her initial comments. The debut episode also featured Cunningham’s blunt assessment of Caitlin Clark’s influence on the league. Hanlen compared Clark’s effect on women’s basketball to the transformative impact Michael Jordan and Tiger Woods had on their sports. Cunningham said the effect should be obvious, even if other stars also contributed to the WNBA’s growth. "I should not get in trouble for knowing the obvious," Cunningham said. "That doesn’t mean there wasn’t greatness before her." "The talent has always, always been there," she added. "But now, us players, we just have the platform and the eyes, and companies want to be a part of something great and something that is growing." Cunningham also offered a list of priorities for the WNBA’s next commissioner. Cathy Engelbert recently announced that she will retire at the end of 2026 after seven years leading the league. The WNBA credited Engelbert with overseeing major increases in attendance, viewership, franchise valuations and media revenue. The league also noted that it is expanding from 12 teams to 18 by 2030. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Cunningham said the next commissioner’s first priority should be ensuring every franchise has an adequate practice facility. "There are teams in the WNBA — which, this is, we are the best league in the entire world — that there are people practicing at, like, YMCAs," Cunningham said. "They’re sharing a court by a curtain when there’s, like, YMCA youth camps going on one side and a team practicing on the other. Is that not insane? A couple teams don’t even have a weight room." Cunningham said some owners were being "very cheap" and failing to provide professional players with appropriate resources. "That should be the bare freaking minimum," she said. She also called for a commissioner who communicates directly with players, remains firm under pressure and can unite a politically divided league. "They need to be bold. They need to be confident," Cunningham said. "We’re not always going to agree, but I think there’s a level of respect that you can have and just being a human, being friendly and nice. I think that’s a really good start." Cunningham said "No Hesitation" will continue focusing on film study, strategy and the personalities driving professional basketball. The program is scheduled to release new episodes each Thursday.

articles.title: Ranking the NBA's Top 10 Trade Targets
articles.summary: Basketball's biggest swap meet, officially known as the 2026 NBA offseason, is ticking toward the final buzzer.
articles.body:
Basketball's biggest swap meet, officially known as the 2026 NBA offseason, is ticking toward the final buzzer.

Kawhi Leonard's potential return up north still needs finalizing , and there's still no resolution on Jalen Duren's restricted free agency, but just about every other notable box on the summer checklist has been ticked. It's mostly cricket chirps on the transaction front.

That won't, of course, last forever. In fact, the trade market could re-open at a moment's notice, as franchises start figuring out what they have—and, maybe more importantly, what they still lack—once training camps open later this month.

That makes this an optimal time to survey the trade landscape and identify ( and rank! ) logical candidates for relocation. The following 10 players have all elicited some manner of trade buzz or at least trade speculation, and they'll be subjectively ranked here by perceived trade value, using everything from established production and contract situations to age and projectable upside.

10. Jimmy Butler III, Golden State Warriors

If the Warriors are in the mood for a significant shakeup—perhaps to convince Stephen Curry to put pen to paper on a contract extension —they'll need to send out a sizable salary to make the money work. Butler's (notably expiring) $56.8 million allotment might be the one, especially with more recovery time needed for his ACL.

While there are no direct indications of the Dubs seeking a Butler blockbuster, ESPN's Brian Windhorst said on The Hoop Collective that "[Butler] could function as a huge expiring contract in a trade."

Butler's market is murky given his age (37 this month) and availability issues, but he could appeal both to clubs looking to free up cap space ahead of 2027 free agency and those eyeing a potential midseason lift from a six-time All-Star with some dynamic playoff runs on his resume.

As the league's lone resident in second-apron territory , the Nuggets are being financially squeezed like no one else. It already cost them promising swingman Peyton Watson, and it's fair to wonder whether Denver might need to keep dealing in order to balance the books.

If the Nuggets could stomach another sacrifice, Gordon might be the most logical choice, if only because Denver's discussions earlier this offseason revealed that Gordon was "drawing the strongest external trade interest," per NBA insider Marc Stein . That passes the smell test, since Gordon's two-way versatility could scratch a number of itches for an interested suitor.

That said, he has had struggles staying on the court (87 appearances the past two seasons combined), and those seem unlikely to dissipate with his 31st birthday fast approaching. He's also just starting a three-year, $103.6 million contract extension, meaning he'll offer some security but also come at a pay rate that could be tricky for win-now shoppers to fit in the budget.

Porter has long loomed as a trade candidate. As an in-prime 28-year-old on a team that's knee-deep in rebuilding waters, the timeline troubles are obvious. Plus, with his production having peaked this past season (career-highs of 24.2 points and 3.4 three-pointers), there might be some strike-while-the-iron's-hot urgency on Brooklyn's end.

Throw in the fact Porter is on an expiring contract (at $40.8 million ), and the trade winds just about knock you off your feet. Barring an extension with Brooklyn , the New York Post 's Brian Lewis said on the Third Apron podcast that he'd "be shocked" if Porter lasts past the deadline without a new deal.

Porter is a 6'10" shotmaker with a career conversion rate of 39.8 percent from distance. His trade appeal, in that sense, is obvious. Then again, if he's functioning primarily as a perimeter specialist—he isn't a playmaker, and his defensive impact is spotty—his skill set reads as awfully limited for someone with a salary this rich.

The Blazers have more starting-caliber backcourt players than starting spots available in the backcourt. They won't stay like this forever.

While The Athletic's Jason Quick previously reported that Portland "does not feel it is essential to unload one of its guards," the report also noted how the Blazers "want more big-man depth and realize they have a logjam." While that could theoretically make anyone a trade candidate, Damian Lillard has yet to return from his Achilles tear, Scoot Henderson would be a major sell-low and the Blazers just bought low on Ja Morant this summer.

So, maybe that leaves Holiday as the odd man out, which might be what the trade market prefers. While he isn't young (36) or cheap ( $34.8 million with a $37.2 million player option for next season), he contributes at both ends, works on or off the ball and has filled a supporting role on two title teams. He can't command a fortune, but he'd almost surely fetch at least a first-round pick.

The Wizards seem fully content with having Davis in The District, but is the feeling mutual? Possibly, but maybe only if the price is right (read: maximum contract-sized). When Davis' name was buzzing about the rumor mill earlier this offseason, Yahoo Sports' Kevin O'Connor relayed there were "rumblings [that Davis is] demanding that full max from Washington but would sign for less if traded to a contender."

So, it might be conditional contentment on Davis' side, meaning things just might boil over if there aren't a few Brinks' trucks sent his way. And, really, why would Washington make that commitment any time soon? Davis needs to prove he can stay upright—he has topped 70 games once since 2017-18—and this roster needs to show whether it has any shot at competing in the increasingly difficult East.

So, maybe The Brow happens to shake loose sooner than later. As a 33-year-old with a shaky injury history and apparently massive contract desires, he won't be for everyone. Those not scared off by those factors could be all the way in, though, since his healthy version remains a defensive asset (All-Defensive first team in 2023-24) and an efficient 20-plus-points scorer.

The Cavs are very much in win-now mode. They invested $370 million in their backcourt combo of Donovan Mitchell and James Harden this offseason, and they coughed up an unprotected future first for the right to pay Peyton Watson another $88 million. You don't stomach these kinds of sacrifices unless you feel you have a realistic chance of capturing the crown.

But what if Cleveland again gets denied entry into the NBA's elite class? Because this core has yet to prove it can compete with the conference's best—it finally reached the conference finals this past season, but was swiftly swept out of them—and that particular bar was raised several times this summer.

If the Cavaliers can't compete, then they can't justify the contract cost. And if they ever make that concession, Allen would be "the most likely" player to move, per Heavy.com's Sean Deveney . While Allen's skill set is fairly limited, his market might be robust. Few rim-runners provide a bigger impact on both ends of the floor than the career 64.1 percent shooter who has thrice received votes for Defensive Player of the Year.

Dallas insists it has zero interest in dealing Irving, but that stance is routinely met with eye-rolling skepticism. As it should be. Even if the Mavericks believe he'd be the ultimate mentor for Cooper Flagg, there's no getting around the 15-year age gap between them and the obvious timeline turbulence that creates.

As ESPN's Tim MacMahon put it, "front offices across the league anticipate that one or both parties could decide it's in their best interest to part ways." That feels more like a when than an if , since Dallas might need a best-case-scenario kind of season just to factor into the Western Conference playoff race.

Scoring-starved, win-now suitors will be hoping it's obvious early that the Mavs can't compete, since Irving will intrigue as a potential one-stop shop to fix any offensive issues. The nine-time All-Star is a dizzying ball-handler, a 50/40/90 club member, a clutch shot-maker and a discerning distributor who offers on-or-off-ball versatility.

Last summer, the Rockets wagered on Durant being their missing-piece addition who could elevate them into full-fledged contention. They wound up suffering the same fate as they did the season prior to his arrival, going exactly 52-30 and losing a first-round series in six games.

Now, that's not to suggest Durant is at fault for the lack of elevation—he was his usual awesomely efficient self—but maybe it has Houston wondering whether its young core can catch up to the 37-year-old (38 this month) future Hall of Famer. Maybe moving him for better long-term assets could be the prudent move to make, although Heavy.com's Sean Deveney cautioned that "Durant is not seen as a top-level commodity by many front offices," so it's unclear what kind of haul Houston would receive.

Then again, it's Kevin freakin' Durant—a living-legend caliber scorer who made All-NBA second team just this past season. Any team with win-now intentions in need of an offensive boost would have to give him a long look, even if he isn't getting younger and lacks contract security past this campaign ( $46.1 million player option for 2027-28).

2. Trey Murphy III, New Orleans Pelicans

There are a lot of players on this list—most ranked lower—with more accolades than Murphy. In terms of name brand, his just doesn't measure up. Except that's not what we're measuring, remember? We're talking trade value, and that's where Murphy has the edge on just about anyone conceivably connected to the market.

He is 26 years old, he fills a coveted role (a three-and-D wing with more scoring punch than the label implies) and he is, relatively speaking, affordable ( $87 million for the next three seasons). The only question is availability, as Yahoo Sports' Kevin O'Connor previously reported the Pelicans "have resisted all trade offers so far and hope to compete next season."

New Orleans, which piled up 117 losses over the past two campaigns, is not at all positioned to compete in the Wild West, so that availability concern might address itself. And as soon as it does, the trade bidding war could be ferocious. He might not be a star—he isn't much of a playmaker or shot-creator—but he is a rock-solid support piece who is efficient and effective in his role.

Putting Garland No. 1 here might raise a few eyebrows. He isn't as accomplished as most of the players on this list, and his connections to the trade market might be the loosest. In short, it's mostly a speculative wager that the Clippers could have to consider a Garland trade to help restock the asset collection after their recent five-first-round-picks punishment .

L.A.'s long-term outlook is now the bleakest in basketball, but letting go of Garland could bring hope of some eventual relief. He wouldn't bring back a blank-check return, but multiple first-round picks feels doable from the right suitor. The 26-year-old is already a two-time All-Star and impresses with both efficient scoring and steady playmaking, but he presumably hasn't exhausted his growth potential yet.

He does have defensive limitations, though, and his injury history is far from spotless. Point guard also isn't a great position of need around the NBA. That said, teams with trouble at the position could see his potential impact being immediate and immense. He's also at the right intersection of age and experience to appeal both to win-now shoppers but also trending-up rebuilders who feel they're on the verge of a breakthrough.

articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham has declared her intention to be the next WNBA Commissioner.

At the end of the 2026 season, current WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert will officially step down from her role following a seven-year stint.

With Engelbert gone, the league is in need of its next commissioner, and there are several names that are being considered right now.

While the executives are discussing that, Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham recently declared her interest in stepping in as a successor to Engelbert.

Sophie Cunningham vows to improve 'insane' thing for WNBA players

During the 'No Hesitation' podcast, Cunningham discussed in detail what her first steps will be if she ever gets the chance to become the leader of the WNBA.

"The more I think about that, I think I should be the commissioner. I think I could. I could get this s___ on the right track. Honestly, the first thing I would do is make sure that every team legit has a functional practice facility.

"There are teams in the WNBA; we are the best league in the entire world; there are people practicing at, like, YMCAs," Cunningham said.

She added, "They're sharing a court by a curtain when there's like, YMCA youth camps going on one side and a team practicing on the other. Like, is that not insane? A couple teams don't even have a weight room. Is that weird?"

Until recently, the WNBA barely had any major interest from basketball fans around the globe. But with that changing, the training facilities of a plethora of teams need an upgrade.

Of course, teams like the New York Liberty and LA Sparks are already building their own dedicated training facilities, but it's still surprising that the top teams in the best women's basketball league did not have these facilities for the longest time.

Right now, Cunningham is 30 years old and still likely has a few years left to play at the highest level, but considering her popularity and ideas, it doesn't seem like a bad move to make her the next WNBA Commissioner.

articles.summary: El canterano madridista, que volvió este verano al club tras probar en la NBA, jugará la próxima temporada en la Penya
articles.body: El Real Madrid ha anunciado la cesión de Eli John Ndiaye al Asisa Joventut para la temporada que está a punto de comenzar. El ala-pívot nacionalizado español de 22 años y 2,04 metros había regresado a la disciplina del conjunto blanco este verano después de probar en la NBA, pero finalmente jugará en la Penya, donde podrá seguir creciendo. Con intención de regresar a la Liga Endesa, Ndiaye tuvo una oferta del Valencia Basket para esta campaña, pero el Real Madrid había inscrito al jugador en el derecho de tanteo hace un año, cuando se marchó a los Hawks. El club blanco igualó la oferta taronja por él y lo reincorporó a su disciplina. Sin embargo, el futuro de Ndiaye era incierto. El puesto de ala-pívot parece bien cubierto en el Madrid con la presencia de los recién llegados Mikael Jantunen y Jaime Pradilla además de Chuma Okeke y Gabriel Deck que ya estaban en la plantilla y también pueden ocupar esa posición. Así que la cesión se contemplaba como opción para que pudiera tener minutos y seguir desarrollándose.
